definition_zh: 地幔；披风，斗篷；覆盖层；承担（职责、衣钵）
definition_en: the rocky layer between Earth's crust and core; also a loose cloak or a covering layer
core_image: 一件厚斗篷从肩头垂下把身体整个裹住，地球内部也有一层岩石斗篷裹住地核
scene: 深洋底下的岩石受热缓慢上升，又向两侧摊开。Hot rock rises through the mantle and spreads beneath the ocean floor.
sceneCN: 这里 mantle 指「地幔」（第 1 个义项：地壳与地核之间的岩石层）；句意为炽热的岩石穿过地幔上升，并在海底之下向两侧扩散。

pos.zh: 地幔；披风；覆盖层；外套膜；纱罩
覆盖；笼罩
（雾、雪等）铺展开来盖住表面

derivatives.zh: 纹章上环绕盾牌的垂饰
小掩体；可移动的防护屏

senses.title: The rocky layer below the crust
senses.titleCN: 地幔：地壳之下的岩石层
senses.definition: the thick layer of hot rock between Earth's crust and its core
senses.definitionCN: 地壳与地核之间的厚层炽热岩石
senses.example: Hot rock rises through the mantle and spreads beneath the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 炽热的岩石穿过地幔上升，并在海底之下向两侧扩散。
senses.why: The geological sense borrows the cloak image: the mantle wraps around the core the way a cloak wraps a body.
senses.whyCN: 地质义借用了「斗篷」的形象：地幔像斗篷裹住身体那样包住地核。

senses.title: A loose cloak
senses.titleCN: 披风：披在肩上的宽大外套
senses.definition: a loose sleeveless cloak worn over other clothes
senses.definitionCN: 披在其他衣服外面的宽松无袖外套
senses.example: She drew her mantle closer against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 她把披风裹紧以挡风。
senses.why: The word entered English as the name of a cloak, and every later sense grows out of that garment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初进入英语时就是「斗篷」的名称，后来所有义项都从这件衣服生长出来。

senses.title: A covering layer
senses.titleCN: 覆盖层：像被子一样盖住表面的东西
senses.definition: a layer of something that covers a surface completely
senses.definitionCN: 完全盖住某一表面的一层东西
senses.example: A mantle of snow lay over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一层白雪覆盖着山谷。
senses.why: A cloak covers a body and snow covers a valley; the shape of covering is the same in both cases.
senses.whyCN: 斗篷盖住身体，雪盖住山谷，两种情形里「覆盖」的形状是一样的。

senses.title: To cover or envelop
senses.definition: to cover something as if with a cloak
senses.definitionCN: 像盖上一件斗篷那样罩住某物
senses.example: Thick fog mantled the harbor at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时浓雾笼罩着港口。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to mantle something is simply to put a mantle on it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成了动词：mantle 某物就是给它盖上一层斗篷。

senses.title: To take on a role or duty
senses.definition: to take on a role, duty or tradition passed down from someone else
senses.definitionCN: 接过别人传下来的角色、职责或传统
senses.example: She took up the mantle of the retiring director.
senses.exampleCN: 她接过了退休主管的职责。
senses.why: The image comes from a cloak handed from one person to another, as a prophet's mantle passes to a successor.
senses.whyCN: 这个形象来自斗篷由一人传给另一人，正如先知的衣钵传给继承者。

senses.title: The mantle of a mollusk
senses.titleCN: 外套膜：软体动物包住内脏的膜
senses.definition: the fold of tissue that lines the shell of a mollusk
senses.definitionCN: 软体动物体内贴着壳的那层组织褶
senses.example: The oyster deposits new shell along its mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 牡蛎沿着外套膜沉积新的壳。
senses.why: Biologists reused the cloak image for the tissue sheet that wraps the animal's body.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借「斗篷」的形象，指包住动物身体的那层组织。

senses.title: A gas mantle
senses.titleCN: 纱罩：燃气灯里发光的网罩
senses.definition: a mesh that glows when a gas flame heats it
senses.definitionCN: 被燃气火焰烧热后发光的网状罩子
senses.example: The old lamp still had a fragile gas mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 那盏旧灯上还装着一个易碎的纱罩。
senses.why: The mesh is a sleeve slipped over the flame, so the cloak image fits again.
senses.whyCN: 网罩是套在火焰外面的套子，斗篷的形象又一次贴合。

senses.title: An abstract veil
senses.definition: something that hides or surrounds a situation, such as secrecy or silence
senses.definitionCN: 遮住或围住某种情形的抽象之物，如保密或沉默
senses.example: The negotiations were wrapped in a mantle of secrecy.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判被一层保密的帷幕包住。
senses.why: When the covering is not physical, mantle names whatever keeps a matter out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 当覆盖物不是实物时，mantle 就指把某件事挡在视线之外的东西。

intro.en: Mantle goes back to a Latin word for a cloak. The clothing sense is old; the geological and biological senses are later extensions of the same covering image. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mantle 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「斗篷」的词。衣物义很古老，地质义与生物义是同一「覆盖」形象的后起延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin mantellum, also written mantum, meant 'a cloak or veil'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; some references suggest a Gaulish or Celtic source for the covering sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mantellum（也写作 mantum）意为「斗篷、面纱」。它更早的来源不确定，有资料认为「覆盖物」这一义可能来自高卢语或凯尔特语。

items.en: The ending of mantellum looks like a diminutive suffix, but whether it really is one remains disputed, so the word is best treated as a single lexical item.
items.cn: mantellum 的词尾看起来像指小后缀，但它是否真是指小形式仍有争议，因此最好把这个词当作一个整体词项处理。

items.en: Old French mantel carried the cloak sense into English, where the spelling later became mantle.
items.cn: 古法语 mantel 把「斗篷」义带入英语，拼写后来固定为 mantle。

items.en: Middle English used mantle for a sleeveless outer garment and already for any protective covering, including figurative ones.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mantle 指无袖外衣，并且已经用它指任何保护性覆盖物，包括比喻用法。

items.en: Geologists extended the cloak image to the rocky layer around the core, while biologists used it for the tissue sheet of mollusks; the phrase 'take up the mantle' comes from the biblical story of Elijah's cloak passing to Elisha.
items.cn: 地质学家把斗篷的形象延伸指包住地核的岩石层，生物学家则用它指软体动物那层组织；短语 take up the mantle 出自《列王纪》中以利亚的斗篷传给以利沙的故事。

note.en: Group one lists words that sound or look close to mantle; group two lists words that also describe a covering, with a different emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是与 mantle 读音或拼写相近的词；第二组是同样表示「覆盖物」但侧重点不同的词。

entries.definition: the shelf above a fireplace. It is a different word with a different spelling: -el, not -le.
entries.definitionCN: 壁炉上方的搁架。它是另一个词，拼写也不同：结尾是 -el，不是 -le。

entries.definition: relating to the mind. The first vowel is /e/, not /æ/, and there is no -tle ending.
entries.definitionCN: 与心理、精神有关的。第一个元音是 /e/ 而不是 /æ/，结尾也不是 -tle。

entries.definition: a praying insect with long front legs. It shares the opening man- but ends in -tis.
entries.definitionCN: 螳螂，前足很长的昆虫。它与 mantle 共享开头 man-，但结尾是 -tis。

entries.definition: to crush or tear something badly. It has a hard /ŋɡ/ in the middle that mantle does not have.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西压坏或撕坏。它中间有 mantle 所没有的 /ŋɡ/ 音。

entries.definition: a sleeveless outer garment, closer to a coat than to a loose mantle; it also means something that hides.
entries.definitionCN: 无袖外衣，比宽松的披风更接近大衣；也可指起遮蔽作用的东西。

entries.definition: a thin cloth worn over the face, or anything that hides a view; the emphasis is on concealment, not warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 遮面的薄纱，或任何挡住视线的东西；重点在「遮蔽」，不在保暖。

entries.definition: a cloth used to wrap a body, or a layer that completely envelops something.
entries.definitionCN: 裹尸布，或把某物完全包住的一层东西。

entries.definition: the neutral word for anything placed over an object; it carries no image of a garment or a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「盖在上面」的中性词，不带衣物或外壳的形象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real spellings, real compounds and real images, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拼写、真实的复合词和真实的形象，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mantle and mantel are homophones: a mantel is the shelf over a fireplace, while a mantle is the cloak; the shelf is a board, the cloak is clothing.
normal.cn: mantle 与 mantel 同音：mantel 是壁炉上的搁架，mantle 是斗篷；搁架是木板，斗篷是衣物。

normal.en: The Earth's mantle is literally the planet's cloak: it wraps around the core and keeps the heat in.
normal.cn: 地幔就是地球的斗篷：它包住地核，把热量留在里面。

normal.en: 'Take up the mantle' comes from the story of Elijah's cloak falling to Elisha, so the phrase means inheriting another person's task.
normal.cn: take up the mantle 出自以利亚的斗篷落到以利沙身上的故事，所以这个短语表示继承他人的事业。

normal.en: A mantle of snow is a blanket of snow: the same word covers a valley and a shoulder.
normal.cn: a mantle of snow 就是一层雪被：同一个词既盖住山谷，也盖住肩膀。

normal.en: A mollusk's mantle is the tissue that lines its shell, like a coat lining the body.
normal.cn: 软体动物的外套膜是贴着壳的那层组织，就像给身体做衬里的外套。

abstract.en: Abstractly, mantle means one layer wrapping another: a core is always inside, and the mantle is always the outermost skin that holds it.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，mantle 表示一层包住另一层：核心总在里面，而 mantle 总是包住它的最外层皮。

abstract.en: From clothing to the Earth to a handed-down duty, the constant is enclosure: something is kept inside a boundary.
abstract.cn: 从衣物到地球再到传下来的职责，不变的是「包围」：某物被留在一个边界之内。

abstract.en: The symbol is a filled circle inside a ring: ○ around ●, the ring being the mantle.
abstract.cn: 符号是一个圆核外面套一个环：○ 包住 ●，外环就是 mantle。

examples.en: Convection in the mantle slowly moves the plates above it.
examples.cn: 地幔中的对流缓慢地推动着上面的板块。

examples.en: He wore a dark mantle over his shoulders.
examples.cn: 他肩上披着一件深色斗篷。

examples.en: After the founder retired, his daughter took up the mantle.
examples.cn: 创始人退休后，他的女儿接过了衣钵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「曼特」—— 曼妙的斗篷披在肩上，把身体整个包住 → mantle 披风、覆盖层、地幔

root: 源自拉丁语 mantellum（斗篷、覆盖物），核心含义是「包在外面的覆盖物」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of mantle. They all keep one shape: an outer layer that wraps a core, whether the core is a body, a flame, a shell or the Earth.
sensesIntro.cn: mantle 的八个义项都保持同一个形状：外层包住内核，无论内核是身体、火焰、贝壳还是地球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an outer layer wrapping a core, from a cloak on a body to rock around the core.
core.cn: 核心意象：外层包住内核，从披在身上的斗篷到包住地核的岩石。

branches.en: CLOTH TO COVER: the cloak becomes any covering layer, then the act of covering.
branches.cn: 从衣物到覆盖：斗篷变成任何覆盖层，再变成覆盖的动作。

branches.en: PHYSICAL SHELLS: the Earth's rocky layer and the glowing mesh both enclose something hot.
branches.cn: 实体外壳：地球的岩石层与发光的网罩都包住某种高温之物。

branches.en: INHERITED ROLE: a cloak passed from one person to another becomes a duty passed down.
branches.cn: 继承的角色：斗篷由一人传给另一人，就变成传下来的职责。

branches.en: BODY TISSUE: biology keeps the wrapping shape but moves it inside the animal.
branches.cn: 身体组织：生物学保留「包裹」的形状，只是把它移到动物体内。

branches.en: ABSTRACT VEIL: when nothing physical is covered, the mantle hides a matter from view.
branches.cn: 抽象帷幕：当没有实物可盖时，mantle 就把一件事挡在视线之外。

intro.en: Mantle is a whole Latin borrowing rather than a native compound, but it still builds a small family of English words and fixed phrases.
intro.cn: mantle 是整个借来的拉丁词，不是英语本族复合词，但它仍构成一小族英语词与固定短语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source mantellum / mantum supplies the base; English adds -ed, -ing and the diminutive -let, and geology adds compound phrases such as mantle plume.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 mantellum / mantum 提供基础；英语加上 -ed、-ing 与指小后缀 -let，地质学再加 mantle plume 这类复合短语。

items.meaning: the base noun borrowed into English as mantle
items.meaningCN: 作为基础名词被借入英语，成为 mantle
items.example: The Latin noun named a cloak worn over the shoulders.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指披在肩上的斗篷。

items.meaning: covered as if by a cloak
items.meaningCN: 被覆盖的（-ed 构成过去分词作形容词）
items.example: The hills were mantled in cloud.
items.exampleCN: 群山被云层覆盖。

items.meaning: drapery arranged around a shield in heraldry
items.meaningCN: 纹章中环绕盾牌的垂饰（-ing 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The coat of arms showed elaborate red mantling.
items.exampleCN: 这枚纹章上有繁复的红色垂饰。

items.meaning: a small protective screen or shelter
items.meaningCN: 小型防护屏或掩体（-let 表示指小）
items.example: The gunners crouched behind a steel mantlet.
items.exampleCN: 炮手蹲在一块钢制小掩体后面。

items.meaning: a rising column of hot rock within the mantle
items.meaningCN: 地幔中上升的热岩柱（名词复合）
items.example: A mantle plume can feed volcanic islands far from a plate edge.
items.exampleCN: 地幔柱可以为远离板块边缘的火山岛提供物质。

items.meaning: slow circulation of hot rock inside the mantle
items.meaningCN: 地幔内部热岩的缓慢环流
items.example: Mantle convection is one driver of plate motion.
items.exampleCN: 地幔对流是板块运动的一种驱动力。

items.meaning: the wedge-shaped mantle between a descending slab and the plate above
items.meaningCN: 俯冲板片与上方板块之间的楔形地幔
items.example: Melting in the mantle wedge feeds arc volcanoes.
items.exampleCN: 地幔楔中的熔融为岛弧火山提供岩浆。

items.meaningCN: 源自地幔的（复合形容词）
items.example: The lava is mantle-derived and rich in magnesium.
items.exampleCN: 这种熔岩源自地幔，富含镁。

items.meaning: rock that belongs to the mantle
items.example: Ophiolites expose mantle rock at the surface.
items.exampleCN: 蛇绿岩把地幔岩石暴露到地表。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 披着斗篷的（中世纪拉丁语形容词）

definition_zh: 岩石圈；由地壳与上地幔顶部组成的刚性外壳
definition_en: the rigid outer shell of a planet, made of the crust and the uppermost mantle
core_image: 一颗石球外面套着一层薄而坚硬的石壳，壳上裂成几块大板
scene: 岩石圈并不整体移动，它早已裂成几块大板。The lithosphere is broken into large plates that move slowly over the softer layer below.
sceneCN: 这里 lithosphere 指「岩石圈」（第 1 个义项：地壳与上地幔顶部组成的刚性外壳）；句意为岩石圈裂成几块大板，在下面较软的层之上缓慢移动。

pos.zh: 岩石圈（地壳与上地幔顶部的刚性部分）

senses.title: The rigid outer shell of a planet
senses.titleCN: 岩石圈：行星的刚性外壳
senses.definition: the rigid outer shell of a planet, made of the crust and the uppermost mantle
senses.definitionCN: 由地壳与上地幔顶部组成的行星刚性外壳
senses.example: The lithosphere is broken into large plates that move slowly over the softer layer below.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈裂成几块大板，在下面较软的层之上缓慢移动。
senses.why: The word joins Greek lithos 'stone' with sphaira 'sphere', so it names the stone sphere around a planet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语 lithos「石头」与 sphaira「球」合在一起，指行星外面那层石头球壳。

senses.title: The layer that carries the plates
senses.definition: the layer whose fragments are the tectonic plates
senses.definitionCN: 其碎块构成构造板块的那一层
senses.example: Each plate is a piece of lithosphere, not a separate sheet of crust.
senses.exampleCN: 每个板块都是岩石圈的一块，而不是单独的一层地壳。
senses.why: Plates are defined mechanically: they are the pieces of the rigid shell, so the shell and the plates are the same material at different scales.
senses.whyCN: 板块是按力学性质界定的：它们是刚性外壳的碎块，所以外壳与板块是同一材料在不同尺度上的说法。

senses.title: Thickness that varies by setting
senses.definition: the part of the shell whose thickness differs under oceans and continents
senses.definitionCN: 这层外壳在海洋之下与大陆之下厚度不同
senses.example: Continental lithosphere can be several times thicker than oceanic lithosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆岩石圈的厚度可以达到大洋岩石圈的好几倍。
senses.why: Old, cold continental roots extend far deeper than young oceanic plates, so the same shell has very different depths.
senses.whyCN: 古老寒冷的大陆根扎得远比年轻的大洋板块深，因此同一层外壳的深度差别很大。

senses.title: Rigid, elastic behaviour
senses.definition: the mechanical property of bending and breaking rather than flowing
senses.definitionCN: 会弯曲、会断裂而不会流动的力学性质
senses.example: The lithosphere bends elastically under the weight of a volcano.
senses.exampleCN: 火山的重压使岩石圈发生弹性弯曲。
senses.why: The key contrast is with the asthenosphere: over long times the shell behaves as a solid, while the layer below can flow.
senses.whyCN: 关键对照是与软流圈的区别：在长时间尺度上这层外壳表现为固体，而下面的层可以流动。

senses.title: The layer above the asthenosphere
senses.definition: the outer shell defined by its position above the weaker asthenosphere
senses.definitionCN: 以位于较软弱的软流圈之上来界定的外壳
senses.example: The boundary between lithosphere and asthenosphere is a change in strength, not in rock type.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈与软流圈的界线是强度的变化，而不是岩石种类的变化。
senses.why: The same rock can belong to either layer; what changes across the boundary is how easily it deforms.
senses.whyCN: 同一种岩石可以属于这两层中的任一层；跨过界线改变的是它变形的难易程度。

senses.title: A planetary shell beyond Earth
senses.titleCN: 地球之外的行星岩石圈
senses.definition: the equivalent rigid shell of another rocky planet or moon
senses.definitionCN: 其他岩石行星或卫星的同类刚性外壳
senses.example: Mars has a thick lithosphere that has barely moved for billions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 火星的岩石圈很厚，数十亿年间几乎没怎么移动。
senses.why: The term is defined by mechanics, so it transfers to any rocky body with a stiff outer layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语按力学性质定义，因此可推广到任何具有坚硬外层的岩石天体。

senses.title: The host of resources and earthquakes
senses.definition: the layer in which most mines, oil fields and shallow earthquakes occur
senses.definitionCN: 大多数矿山、油田与浅源地震所在的层
senses.example: Most earthquakes begin within the lithosphere, where rock is brittle enough to break.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数地震始于岩石圈内，那里的岩石足够脆，会断裂。
senses.why: Brittle failure requires a stiff material, so the rigid shell is where faults slip and where resources are dug out.
senses.whyCN: 脆性破坏需要坚硬的材料，因此断层在这层刚性外壳里滑动，资源也从这里开采。

senses.title: The object of lithospheric study
senses.definition: the shell as a subject of geophysics, geochemistry and plate reconstruction
senses.definitionCN: 作为地球物理、地球化学与板块重建研究对象的这层外壳
senses.example: Lithospheric studies combine seismic imaging with heat-flow measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈研究把地震成像与热流测量结合起来。
senses.why: Once a layer is named, it becomes a research object with its own methods and its own adjective, lithospheric.
senses.whyCN: 一层一旦被命名，就成为有自己方法和形容词 lithospheric 的研究对象。

intro.en: Lithosphere is a scientific compound coined from two Greek nouns. The parts are transparent and the meaning has stayed stable since the term was formed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lithosphere 是由两个希腊名词构成的科学复合词。构词成分清楚，术语形成以来含义一直稳定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek lithos meant 'stone', and sphaira meant 'ball, sphere'; both are common in scientific compounds.
items.cn: 希腊语 lithos 意为「石头」，sphaira 意为「球、球体」；两者在科学复合词中都很常见。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists needed a name for the solid outer shell of the planet and combined the two Greek nouns.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学家需要给行星的固体外壳命名，就把这两个希腊名词组合起来。

items.en: The English term spread with the growth of geophysics; its modern definition depends on strength, not on chemical composition.
items.cn: 这个英语术语随地球物理的发展而传播；它的现代定义取决于力学强度，而不是化学成分。

items.en: Plate tectonics gave the word a central role: the lithosphere is the layer that breaks into plates and slides over the asthenosphere.
items.cn: 板块构造学说赋予这个词核心地位：岩石圈就是裂成板块并在软流圈上滑动的那一层。

items.en: The paired term asthenosphere was coined later to name the weaker layer below, so the two words are defined against each other.
items.cn: 与之配套的术语 asthenosphere 后来才出现，用来命名下面较软弱的层，因此这两个词是相互对照定义的。

note.en: Group one collects the other -sphere words that are constantly mixed up; group two collects the geological units that sit next to lithosphere in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是极易混淆的其他 -sphere 词；第二组是语义上与岩石圈相邻的地质单位。

entries.definition: the envelope of gases around a planet. It shares the -sphere ending but begins with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 行星周围的气体层。它共享 -sphere 结尾，但开头是另一个词根。

entries.definition: the zone where living things exist. The first element is Greek bios 'life', not lithos 'stone'.
entries.definitionCN: 生物生存的圈层。前半部分是希腊语 bios「生命」，不是 lithos「石头」。

entries.definition: all the water on a planet. The first element is Greek hydor 'water'.
entries.definitionCN: 行星上的全部水体。前半部分是希腊语 hydor「水」。

entries.definition: a print made by lithography. It shares litho- 'stone' but ends with -graph 'write', not -sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 石版印刷品。它共享 litho-「石头」，但结尾是 -graph「写」，不是 -sphere。

entries.definition: the outermost rocky skin of a planet, thinner than the lithosphere and included within it.
entries.definitionCN: 行星最外面的岩石薄壳，比岩石圈薄，并且包含在岩石圈之内。

entries.definition: one large piece of the lithosphere that moves as a unit.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石圈中作为整体运动的一大块。

entries.definition: the weaker layer beneath the lithosphere, which can flow slowly.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石圈之下较软弱、可以缓慢流动的层。

entries.definition: any outer covering; it describes the shape but carries no geological definition.
entries.definitionCN: 任何外壳；它只描述形状，不含地质学定义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek roots and real layer names, so each word can be decoded rather than merely rhymed.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的圈层名称，因此每个词可以拆解，而不是只靠押韵。

normal.en: litho- means stone and -sphere means ball, so lithosphere is the stone ball around a planet.
normal.cn: litho- 表示石头，-sphere 表示球，所以 lithosphere 就是行星外面那层石头球壳。

normal.en: The four -sphere words form a set: atmosphere is air, hydrosphere is water, biosphere is life, lithosphere is stone.
normal.cn: 四个 -sphere 词构成一组：atmosphere 是气，hydrosphere 是水，biosphere 是生命，lithosphere 是石头。

normal.en: The lithosphere is the plate itself; the crust is only its top layer, so a plate is thicker than a crust.
normal.cn: 岩石圈就是板块本身；地壳只是它的最上层，所以板块比地壳厚。

normal.en: The boundary with the asthenosphere is a strength boundary, not a rock-type boundary.
normal.cn: 与软流圈的界线是强度界线，不是岩石种类界线。

normal.en: Earthquakes and mines cluster in the lithosphere because brittle rock breaks and holds ore.
normal.cn: 地震与矿山集中在岩石圈，因为脆性岩石会断裂，也能储存矿石。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the lithosphere is a cracked eggshell: hard, thin, and divided into pieces that can slide.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，岩石圈像一层裂开的蛋壳：坚硬、很薄，并分成可以滑动的碎块。

abstract.en: The image pairs hardness with thinness: what makes it a plate is that it can break rather than flow.
abstract.cn: 这个形象把「硬」与「薄」配在一起：使它成为板块的，正是它会断裂而不是流动。

abstract.en: Symbol: a thin hard ring around a soft inner circle, with cracks across the ring.
abstract.cn: 符号：软内圈外面套一层薄硬的环，环上布满裂缝。

examples.en: Oceanic lithosphere is created at mid-ocean ridges and destroyed at trenches.
examples.cn: 大洋岩石圈在大洋中脊生成，在海沟处消亡。

examples.en: The lithosphere behaves as a rigid plate over long time spans.
examples.cn: 在长时间尺度上，岩石圈表现为刚性板块。

examples.en: Scientists map the base of the lithosphere using seismic waves.
examples.cn: 科学家用地震波绘制岩石圈的底部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里索斯菲尔」—— 石头（litho）做的球（sphere） → lithosphere 岩石圈

root: 由希腊语 lithos（石头）与 sphaira（球）组合而成，字面义为「石头球壳」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of lithosphere. The thread is a hard outer shell: it carries the plates, bends elastically, and sits on a softer layer.
sensesIntro.cn: lithosphere 的八个义项。主线是一层坚硬外壳：它承载板块、发生弹性弯曲，并坐在较软的层之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin hard shell around a soft interior, cracked into moving pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：软内部外面一层薄硬壳，壳裂成会移动的碎块。

branches.en: SHELL AND THICKNESS: the same hard shell is thin under oceans and thick under old continents.
branches.cn: 外壳与厚度：同一层硬壳在海洋下很薄，在古老大陆下很厚。

branches.en: PLATE IDENTITY: a plate is not a separate crust but a fragment of this shell.
branches.cn: 板块同一性：板块不是另一层地壳，而是这层外壳的碎块。

branches.en: STRENGTH BOUNDARY: rigidity is measured against the softer layer below.
branches.cn: 强度界线：刚性是相对于下面较软的层来衡量的。

branches.en: PLANETARY TRANSFER: the mechanical definition works on any rocky body.
branches.cn: 行星推广：这一定义按力学性质成立，因此适用于任何岩石天体。

branches.en: HUMAN USE: the same shell holds ore, breaks in earthquakes and becomes an object of study.
branches.cn: 人类利用：同一层外壳储存矿石、在地震中破裂，也成为研究对象。

intro.en: Lithosphere is a compound of two Greek nouns, and both parts recur across scientific English, so the word is easy to decode and easy to extend.
intro.cn: lithosphere 由两个希腊名词复合而成，两部分在科学英语中反复出现，因此这个词既好拆解也便于扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: the elements are Greek lithos and sphaira, combined in modern scientific coinage, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源：构词成分是希腊语 lithos 与 sphaira，在现代科技术语中组合而成，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: Lithology is the study of rock types.
items.exampleCN: 岩性学研究岩石类型。

items.example: The atmosphere is the gaseous sphere of a planet.
items.exampleCN: 大气层是行星的气体圈层。

items.meaningCN: 与岩石圈有关的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: Lithospheric plates move a few centimetres a year.
items.exampleCN: 岩石圈板块每年移动几厘米。

items.meaningCN: 岩石类型研究（-logy 表示学科）
items.example: The drill core changed lithology at two hundred metres.
items.exampleCN: 钻芯在两百米处岩性发生变化。

items.meaningCN: 使沉积物变成岩石（-ify 表示使成为）
items.example: Pressure and cementation lithify loose sand.
items.exampleCN: 压力与胶结作用把松砂变成岩石。

items.meaning: made of stone; relating to stone
items.example: Archaeologists found lithic tools in the cave.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家在洞中发现了石制工具。

items.meaning: a rigid fragment of the lithosphere
items.meaningCN: 岩石圈的一块刚性碎块
items.example: Each lithosphere plate carries both crust and upper mantle.
items.exampleCN: 每个岩石圈板块都带着地壳与上地幔。

items.meaning: the depth where the rigid shell meets the weaker layer
items.meaningCN: 刚性外壳与较软层相接的深度（复合术语）
items.example: The lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary lies near one hundred kilometres under oceans.
items.exampleCN: 大洋之下的岩石圈与软流圈界面约在一百公里深处。

definition_zh: 软流圈；上地幔中可以缓慢流动的软弱层
definition_en: the weak, slowly flowing layer of the upper mantle beneath the lithosphere
core_image: 坚硬石板下面垫着一层温热的软蜡，石板能在上面缓慢滑动
scene: 坚硬石板下面那层岩石虽然仍是固体，却能在漫长时间里缓慢流动。The asthenosphere flows slowly, allowing the plates above to slide.
sceneCN: 这里 asthenosphere 指「软流圈」（第 1 个义项：上地幔中可以缓慢流动的软弱层）；句意为软流圈缓慢流动，使上面的板块得以滑动。

pos.zh: 软流圈（岩石圈之下的软弱层）

senses.title: The weak layer of the upper mantle
senses.titleCN: 软流圈：上地幔中的软弱层
senses.definition: the weak, slowly flowing layer of the upper mantle beneath the lithosphere
senses.definitionCN: 岩石圈之下、上地幔中可以缓慢流动的软弱层
senses.example: The asthenosphere flows slowly, allowing the plates above to slide.
senses.exampleCN: 软流圈缓慢流动，使上面的板块得以滑动。
senses.why: Greek asthenes means 'weak', so the word names the layer that is mechanically weak even though it is still solid rock.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 asthenes 意为「软弱」，所以这个词命名的是力学上软弱的层，尽管它仍是固体岩石。

senses.title: A layer that deforms plastically
senses.definition: the layer that changes shape by flowing instead of breaking
senses.definitionCN: 以流动而非断裂来改变形状的那一层
senses.example: Over thousands of years, the asthenosphere deforms like extremely stiff putty.
senses.exampleCN: 在数千年尺度上，软流圈像极硬的油灰一样变形。
senses.why: Weakness here is about time: a material can be solid to a hammer and still flow over geological time.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「软弱」与时间尺度有关：对锤子而言是固体，在地质时间尺度上却能流动。

senses.title: The lubricating base of plate motion
senses.definition: the layer that lets rigid plates slide horizontally
senses.definitionCN: 让刚性板块水平滑动的那一层
senses.example: Plates move because the asthenosphere beneath them can yield.
senses.exampleCN: 板块能移动，是因为它们下面的软流圈可以让位。
senses.why: A rigid plate cannot slide on rigid rock; it needs a layer that can flow out of the way.
senses.whyCN: 刚性板块无法在刚性岩石上滑动，它需要一层能流动让位的物质。

senses.title: A source region for magma
senses.definition: the layer where decompression and partial melting produce magma
senses.definitionCN: 减压与部分熔融产生岩浆的那一层
senses.example: Magma rises from partial melting in the asthenosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆来自软流圈中的部分熔融。
senses.why: Rising hot rock enters lower pressure, melts a little, and the melt separates from the solid residue.
senses.whyCN: 上升的热岩进入低压区，少量熔融，熔体便与固体残余分离。

senses.title: The seismic low-velocity zone
senses.definition: the zone where seismic waves slow down because the rock is near its melting point
senses.definitionCN: 因岩石接近熔点而使地震波减速的带
senses.example: Seismic waves slow sharply when they enter the asthenosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 地震波进入软流圈时明显减速。
senses.why: Heat and partial melt soften the rock, so elastic waves travel more slowly through it.
senses.whyCN: 热量与部分熔融使岩石变软，弹性波在其中传播得更慢。

senses.title: A depth range, not a fixed line
senses.titleCN: 一个深度范围，而非固定界线
senses.definition: the depth band whose top and bottom change with heat flow and plate age
senses.definitionCN: 上下界随热流与板块年龄变化的深度带
senses.example: Under old continents the asthenosphere begins deeper than under young oceans.
senses.exampleCN: 古老大陆之下的软流圈比年轻大洋之下开始得更深。
senses.why: The layer is defined by temperature and pressure, so its boundaries move with the thermal state of the region.
senses.whyCN: 这层由温度与压力界定，因此它的界线会随该区的热状态而变化。

senses.title: The contrast layer to the lithosphere
senses.definition: the layer understood mainly as the opposite of the rigid lithosphere
senses.definitionCN: 主要作为刚性岩石圈的对立面来理解的那一层
senses.example: The two names describe strength, not two different kinds of rock.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个名称描述的是强度，而不是两种不同的岩石。
senses.why: Asthenosphere and lithosphere are a paired vocabulary: each word gets its meaning from the contrast with the other.
senses.whyCN: 软流圈与岩石圈是一对配套词汇：每个词的含义都来自与另一个词的对照。

senses.title: A weak layer on other rocky planets
senses.titleCN: 其他岩石行星上的软弱层
senses.definition: the inferred equivalent layer inside another rocky body
senses.definitionCN: 在其他岩石天体内部推测存在的同类软弱层
senses.example: Some models give Venus an asthenosphere, though the evidence is indirect.
senses.exampleCN: 有些模型认为金星也有软流圈，但证据是间接的。
senses.why: Because the definition is mechanical, it can be applied to any hot rocky body whose outer shell can move.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个定义按力学性质给出，它可以套用到任何外壳能移动的高温岩石天体上。

intro.en: Asthenosphere is a modern scientific compound built from Greek words for 'weak' and 'sphere'. The term was proposed in the early twentieth century as the partner of lithosphere. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: asthenosphere 是现代科学复合词，由希腊语中表示「软弱」与「球」的词构成。这个词在二十世纪初被提出，作为 lithosphere 的配套术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek asthenes meant 'weak, without strength', built from a- 'not' plus sthenos 'strength'; sphaira meant 'ball, sphere'.
items.cn: 希腊语 asthenes 意为「软弱、没有力气」，由 a-「不」加 sthenos「力量」构成；sphaira 意为「球」。

items.en: Geologist Joseph Barrell proposed the term in a series of papers on the strength of the Earth's outer layers.
items.cn: 地质学家约瑟夫·巴雷尔在一系列讨论地球外层强度的论文中提出了这个术语。

items.en: English adopted the term together with lithosphere, and the two words were defined as a mechanical pair.
items.cn: 英语把这个词与 lithosphere 一同引入，并把两个词定义为一对力学概念。

items.en: Seismic studies identified the layer with a low-velocity zone, giving the theoretical term a measurable signature.
items.cn: 地震研究把这层与低速带对应起来，使这个理论术语有了可测量的标志。

items.en: The name says 'weak', but the layer is not liquid; it is solid rock that flows only over very long times.
items.cn: 名称说的是「软弱」，但这层并不是液体；它是只有在极长时间尺度上才流动的固体岩石。

note.en: Group one holds the -sphere terms and the Greek 'weakness' word that are easily confused; group two holds the neighbouring geological units.
note.cn: 第一组是易混的 -sphere 术语与希腊语「软弱」词；第二组是相邻的地质单位。

entries.definition: the rigid outer shell above the asthenosphere; the two words are defined as opposites.
entries.definitionCN: 软流圈之上那层刚性外壳；两个词是作为对立面定义的。

entries.definition: the gas envelope of a planet. It begins with a different root and has nothing to do with rock strength.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的气体包层。开头词根不同，与岩石强度无关。

entries.definition: the zone of living things, built on Greek bios 'life'.
entries.definitionCN: 生物生存的圈层，构词基于希腊语 bios「生命」。

entries.definition: a medical term for weakness or loss of strength; it shares the Greek root but is not a layer name.
entries.definitionCN: 表示虚弱、无力的医学术语；它共享希腊词根，但不是圈层名称。

entries.definition: the whole rocky layer between crust and core; the asthenosphere is only its weak upper part.
entries.definitionCN: 地壳与地核之间的整个岩石层；软流圈只是其中软弱的上部。

entries.definition: molten rock; the asthenosphere is mostly solid and contains only small amounts of melt.
entries.definitionCN: 熔融的岩石；软流圈大部分是固体，只含少量熔体。

entries.definition: the seismic name for the layer, defined by slower wave speeds rather than by chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 这层的地震学名称，按波速变慢而非化学成分来界定。

entries.definition: the thin rocky skin above the mantle; it is far above the asthenosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 地幔之上的岩石薄壳，位置远在软流圈之上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek roots and real physical behaviour, so the memory rests on meaning rather than sound alone.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的物理行为，因此记忆建立在意义上，而不只是声音上。

normal.en: asthenes means weak, so the asthenosphere is the weak sphere under the strong shell.
normal.cn: asthenes 表示软弱，所以 asthenosphere 就是坚硬外壳下面的软弱圈层。

normal.en: The asthenosphere and lithosphere are a pair: weak below, strong above, like putty under a stone slab.
normal.cn: 软流圈与岩石圈是一对：下软上硬，像石板下面的油灰。

normal.en: A low-velocity zone is the seismic fingerprint of the asthenosphere, because soft rock slows waves.
normal.cn: 低速带是软流圈的地震学指纹，因为软岩石会让波速变慢。

normal.en: The layer is solid, not liquid: it flows only over geological time, which is why plates move slowly.
normal.cn: 这层是固体而非液体：它只在漫长地质时间里流动，所以板块运动得很慢。

normal.en: Magma is born where the asthenosphere melts a little as pressure drops.
normal.cn: 压力降低时软流圈少量熔融，岩浆就在这里诞生。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the asthenosphere is a yielding base: a surface can be hard while what supports it is soft.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，软流圈是一层会让步的底座：表面可以很硬，而支撑它的东西很软。

abstract.en: Its lesson is that strength depends on the timescale: the same material is a solid to a hammer and a fluid to a continent.
abstract.cn: 它给出的启示是强度取决于时间尺度：同一种材料对锤子是固体，对大陆是流体。

abstract.en: Symbol: a rigid plate resting on a slowly flowing band, arrows in the band pointing sideways.
abstract.cn: 符号：硬板压在一条缓慢流动的带上，带中的箭头指向两侧。

examples.en: The asthenosphere lies beneath the rigid plates of the lithosphere.
examples.cn: 软流圈位于岩石圈的刚性板块之下。

examples.en: Partial melting in the asthenosphere supplies magma to mid-ocean ridges.
examples.cn: 软流圈中的部分熔融为大洋中脊提供岩浆。

examples.en: Seismic data show the asthenosphere as a zone of reduced wave speed.
examples.cn: 地震数据显示软流圈是一个波速降低的带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿斯软」—— 阿斯泰尼亚是无力，软弱的那层球壳 → asthenosphere 软流圈

root: 由希腊语 asthenes（软弱）与 sphaira（球）组合而成，字面义为「软弱的球层」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of asthenosphere. The thread is a weak layer: solid yet flowing, slow in waves, and yielding enough for plates to slide.
sensesIntro.cn: asthenosphere 的八个义项。主线是一层软弱的层：它是固体却能流动，波速慢，软到足以让板块滑动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm weak band under a hard shell, yielding so the shell can move.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳下面一条温热软弱的带，因让步而使外壳能够移动。

branches.en: PAIRED LAYERS: the name exists only in contrast with the rigid lithosphere.
branches.cn: 成对圈层：这个名称只在同刚性岩石圈的对照中存在。

branches.en: TIME AND DEPTH: weakness is a matter of timescale, and the layer's limits move with heat.
branches.cn: 时间与深度：软弱是时间尺度问题，而这一层的界线随热量移动。

branches.en: SLIDING BASE: plates need something that can get out of the way.
branches.cn: 滑动底座：板块需要一种能让位的物质。

branches.en: MELT AND WAVES: heat softens the rock, so waves slow down and magma can form.
branches.cn: 熔融与波速：热量软化岩石，于是波速变慢，岩浆可以生成。

branches.en: PLANETARY EXTENSION: the mechanical definition can be carried to other rocky bodies.
branches.cn: 行星推广：这一力学定义可以套用到其他岩石天体。

intro.en: Asthenosphere is a Greek compound in modern dress: a negative prefix, a root for strength and a root for sphere. The parts also build medical and scientific vocabulary.
intro.cn: asthenosphere 是披着现代外衣的希腊复合词：一个否定前缀、一个「力量」词根和一个「球」词根。这些成分也构成医学与科学词汇。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek, not Latin: a- 'not' plus sthenos 'strength', and sphaira 'sphere'. There is no Latin cognate family here, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语而非拉丁语：a-「不」加 sthenos「力量」，再加 sphaira「球」。这里没有拉丁同族词族，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.meaningCN: 不；没有（希腊语否定前缀）
items.example: Atypical means not typical.
items.exampleCN: atypical 表示非典型的。

items.example: The root appears in words about strength and weakness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在表示强壮与虚弱的词里。

items.example: The root supplies the -sphere of many layer names.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供了许多圈层名称中的 -sphere。

items.meaningCN: 虚弱；无力（-ia 构成状态名词）
items.example: Muscular asthenia made walking difficult.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉无力使行走困难。

items.example: The patient had an asthenic build.
items.exampleCN: 这位病人体格虚弱。

items.example: Asthenospheric flow drags the base of the plate.
items.exampleCN: 软流圈的流动拖动着板块底部。

items.meaning: a rising flow of weak mantle rock
items.example: Asthenosphere upwelling lifts the surface into a dome.
items.exampleCN: 软流圈上涌把地表抬升成穹隆。

items.meaning: the depth where the weak layer meets the rigid shell
items.meaningCN: 软弱层与刚性外壳相接的深度
items.example: The asthenosphere-lithosphere boundary is mapped by seismic methods.
items.exampleCN: 软流圈与岩石圈界面用地震方法测绘。

definition_zh: 地质构造的；地壳大尺度运动的；建筑构造的；（比喻）根本性的
definition_en: relating to the structure and large-scale movement of the Earth's crust, or to construction
core_image: 木匠把一根根木料搭成整体骨架，岩层也被巨大的力量搭成褶皱与断裂的骨架
scene: 古老海床被缓慢抬升，成了一片高原。A tectonic uplift raised the ancient seabed into a plateau.
sceneCN: 这里 tectonic 指「地壳构造运动的」（第 1 个义项：与地壳大尺度变形有关的）；句意为一次构造抬升把古老海床抬成了一片高原。

pos.zh: 地质构造的；地壳运动的；建筑构造的；（比喻）根本性的

collocations.zh: 构造位移；（比喻）根本性转变

derivatives.zh: 构造作用；地壳构造运动

senses.title: Relating to crustal structure
senses.definition: relating to the structure and large-scale deformation of the Earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 与地壳的结构及大尺度变形有关的
senses.example: A tectonic uplift raised the ancient seabed into a plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 一次构造抬升把古老海床抬成了一片高原。
senses.why: The Greek root tekton means 'builder', so tectonic describes how the crust is built and rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 tekton 意为「建造者」，所以 tectonic 描述地壳如何被搭起与重建。

senses.title: Relating to plate motion
senses.definition: relating to the movement and interaction of lithospheric plates
senses.definitionCN: 与岩石圈板块的运动和相互作用有关的
senses.example: Tectonic plates carry continents thousands of kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 构造板块把大陆搬运数千公里。
senses.why: Once the crust is seen as built from plates, every plate interaction is a tectonic process.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把地壳看作由板块搭成，每一次板块相互作用都是构造过程。

senses.title: Relating to mountain building
senses.definition: relating to the forces that raise mountain belts
senses.definitionCN: 与抬升山脉的那些力有关的
senses.example: The tectonic belt runs along the collision zone.
senses.exampleCN: 这条构造带沿碰撞带延伸。
senses.why: Mountains are the visible result of crust being compressed and thickened, so the adjective covers the whole process.
senses.whyCN: 山脉是地壳受挤压增厚的可见结果，因此这个形容词覆盖整个造山过程。

senses.title: Relating to building or construction
senses.definition: relating to construction and the way a building is put together
senses.definitionCN: 与建造以及建筑如何组装有关的
senses.example: Architects study tectonic form, the visible logic of how a building is assembled.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师研究构造形式，即建筑如何组装的可见逻辑。
senses.why: This is the older sense: tekton is a carpenter or builder, and architecture inherited the word for the art of joining parts.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的义项：tekton 就是木匠或建造者，建筑学继承这个词，用来指拼接构件的技艺。

senses.title: A structural, far-reaching change
senses.titleCN: 比喻：结构性的、根本性的变化
senses.definition: used figuratively for changes that reshape the basic structure of something
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指重塑某事物基本结构的变化
senses.example: The internet caused a tectonic shift in how people shop.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网改变了人们购物的基本结构。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the scale of plate motion: slow, huge, and impossible to reverse once it starts.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了板块运动的尺度：缓慢、巨大，一旦开始就难以逆转。

senses.title: The adjective of tectonics
senses.definition: the adjective used in the names of subfields and processes of tectonics
senses.definitionCN: 用于构造学各分支与过程名称的形容词
senses.example: Tectonic studies combine field mapping with geophysics.
senses.exampleCN: 构造研究把野外填图与地球物理结合起来。
senses.why: Every discipline needs an adjective for its subject, so tectonic modifies studies, maps, models and events.
senses.whyCN: 每个学科都需要一个修饰其研究对象的形容词，于是 tectonic 修饰研究、图件、模型与事件。

senses.title: Visible construction logic in art
senses.definition: in art and design, describing the expressed logic of how parts support one another
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术与设计中，描述各部件如何相互支撑的可见逻辑
senses.example: The sculptor left the tectonic joints of the frame exposed.
senses.exampleCN: 雕塑家把框架的构造接点露在外面。
senses.why: A building shows its bones honestly when the joints are visible; critics borrowed tectonic for that honesty.
senses.whyCN: 当接点可见时，建筑就诚实地露出骨架；评论家借 tectonic 指这种诚实。

senses.title: Relating to structural earthquakes
senses.definition: describing earthquakes caused by crustal faulting rather than by volcanoes or collapse
senses.definitionCN: 描述由地壳断裂而非火山或塌陷引起的地震
senses.example: Most damaging quakes are tectonic rather than volcanic.
senses.exampleCN: 破坏性大的地震多是构造地震，而不是火山地震。
senses.why: Classifying a quake as tectonic is saying its cause is the building and breaking of the crust.
senses.whyCN: 把地震归为构造地震，就是说它的成因是地壳的搭建与破裂。

intro.en: Tectonic comes from Greek tekton 'builder, carpenter'. Architecture kept the older sense of construction, while geology took the word for the building of the crust. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tectonic 来自希腊语 tekton「建造者、木匠」。建筑学保留了「建造」的旧义，地质学则用这个词指地壳的搭建。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek tekton meant 'builder, carpenter, craftsman', and tektonike techne meant 'the art of building'; the verb tekein meant 'to build, produce'.
items.cn: 希腊语 tekton 意为「建造者、木匠、工匠」，tektonike techne 意为「建造的艺术」；动词 tekein 意为「建造、制作」。

items.en: Tektonikos meant 'skilled in building, relating to construction', which is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: tektonikos 意为「擅长建造的、与构造有关的」，是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: Scientific Latin took tectonicus for structural descriptions, and European geology used it for the architecture of the crust.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语用 tectonicus 描述结构，欧洲地质学则用它指地壳的架构。

items.en: English geology adopted tectonic for the formation of folds, faults and mountain belts.
items.cn: 英语地质学采用 tectonic 指褶皱、断层与山脉带的形成。

items.en: Plate tectonics made the adjective everyday scientific vocabulary, and figurative uses such as tectonic shift spread into general speech.
items.cn: 板块构造学说使这个形容词成为常用科学词汇，而 tectonic shift 这类比喻用法也进入日常语言。

items.en: The deeper origin of tekein is reconstructed rather than attested; a common proposal links it to a root meaning 'to weave or fabricate'.
items.cn: tekein 的更早来源是重构而非有记录的；常见的一种假说把它连到一个意为「编织、制作」的词根上。

note.en: Group one holds words that differ from tectonic by a few sounds or letters; group two holds adjectives that also describe large-scale Earth structure.
note.cn: 第一组是与 tectonic 在读音或字母上只差一点的词；第二组是同样描述地球大尺度结构的形容词。

entries.definition: a technique or technical detail; it is built on the same Greek root but means skill, not crustal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 技巧或技术细节；它同出希腊词根，但指技能，不指地壳结构。

entries.definition: the field or process noun; tectonic is the adjective, tectonics the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 学科或过程名词；tectonic 是形容词，tectonics 是名词。

entries.definition: giving strength or tone; the first syllable is not tek- and there is no -nic ending.
entries.definitionCN: 起强壮或提振作用的；第一音节不是 tek-，也没有 -nic 结尾。

entries.definition: a plan for achieving something; it has /tæk/ at the start, not /tek/.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成目标而制定的策略；开头是 /tæk/ 而不是 /tek/。

entries.definition: relating to structure in any field; it is the neutral word, while tectonic is tied to the Earth's crust or to building.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何领域的结构有关；它是中性词，而 tectonic 专指地壳或建筑。

entries.definition: relating to geology as a whole, including rocks, fossils and time; tectonic is only the structural part.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个地质学有关，包括岩石、化石与时间；tectonic 只涉及构造部分。

entries.definition: relating specifically to the crust; tectonic can involve the upper mantle as well.
entries.definitionCN: 专指地壳的；而 tectonic 也可涉及上地幔。

entries.definition: relating to mountain building; tectonic is wider and covers rifting and plate motion too.
entries.definitionCN: 专指造山的；tectonic 范围更广，也包括裂谷与板块运动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek roots and real architectural links, so the word can be rebuilt from its parts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的建筑学关联，因此这个词可以从构件重建。

normal.en: tekton means builder, so tectonic is about how the Earth is built: plates, folds and faults.
normal.cn: tekton 表示建造者，所以 tectonic 讲的是地球如何被搭建：板块、褶皱与断层。

normal.en: Architecture uses tectonic for visible construction logic, which is the same root as geology's usage.
normal.cn: 建筑学用 tectonic 指可见的构造逻辑，这与地质学的用法同出一个词根。

normal.en: tectonic is the adjective and tectonics is the noun, just as economic pairs with economics.
normal.cn: tectonic 是形容词，tectonics 是名词，正如 economic 与 economics 的配对。

normal.en: A tectonic shift is slow and enormous, which is why the phrase works for social change.
normal.cn: 构造位移缓慢而巨大，所以这个短语也适用于社会变化。

normal.en: A tectonic earthquake comes from faulting, not from a volcano, so the label names the cause.
normal.cn: 构造地震来自断层活动而非火山，所以这个标签指的是成因。

abstract.en: Abstractly, tectonic means built and rebuilt: a structure is assembled, stressed, and then reassembled.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，tectonic 表示搭建与重建：结构被组装、受力，然后重新组装。

abstract.en: The metaphor scales: a carpenter joins beams, the Earth joins plates, a society joins institutions, and all can shift.
abstract.cn: 这个比喻可以缩放：木匠拼接梁木，地球拼接板块，社会拼接制度，而它们都会位移。

abstract.en: Symbol: two arrows pressing a layered stack into folds, with a joint line where the layers meet.
abstract.cn: 符号：两个箭头把层叠的岩层压成褶皱，层与层相接处留一条接缝线。

examples.en: Tectonic forces built the mountain range over millions of years.
examples.cn: 构造力在数百万年间造就了这条山脉。

examples.en: The region is tectonically active and has many small earthquakes.
examples.cn: 该地区构造活动活跃，有许多小地震。

examples.en: The merger produced a tectonic change in the industry.
examples.cn: 这次合并使行业发生了根本性变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泰克托尼」—— 泰克是技术，托尼是木匠名，木匠搭骨架 → tectonic 构造的

root: 源自希腊语 tekton（建造者、木匠）及其形容词 tektonikos，核心含义是「与建造、构架有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tectonic. The core is construction: the crust is built into plates and folds, and buildings are built into visible frames.
sensesIntro.cn: tectonic 的八个义项。核心是「建造」：地壳被搭成板块与褶皱，建筑被搭成可见的骨架。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a builder joining parts into a frame, applied to rock layers and to buildings.
core.cn: 核心意象：建造者把构件拼成骨架，这一形象既用于岩层，也用于建筑。

branches.en: CRUST AS A FRAME: structure is the base meaning, and the adjective names the field.
branches.cn: 地壳即骨架：结构是基础义，这个形容词为这一领域命名。

branches.en: BUILDING THE EARTH: plates move, and their collisions raise mountains.
branches.cn: 建造地球：板块移动，板块碰撞抬起山脉。

branches.en: VISIBLE CONSTRUCTION: architecture and art keep the literal craft sense.
branches.cn: 可见的建造：建筑与艺术保留了字面上的工艺义。

branches.en: METAPHOR OF SCALE: slow, huge structural change borrows the image of moving plates.
branches.cn: 尺度的比喻：缓慢而巨大的结构变化借用了板块移动的形象。

branches.en: CAUSE LABEL: a tectonic earthquake is named for how the crust broke.
branches.cn: 成因标签：构造地震按地壳如何破裂来命名。

intro.en: Tectonic is built on a Greek root for building, with suffixes that turn it into a noun, an adverb and a field name.
intro.cn: tectonic 建立在希腊语「建造」词根上，后缀把它变成名词、副词与学科名称。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek tekton and tektonikos, loaned into scientific Latin as tectonicus. There is no separate Latin root family, so latinEntries stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语 tekton 与 tektonikos，后被借入科学拉丁语作 tectonicus。这里没有另一支拉丁词根族，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.meaning: one who builds or joins materials
items.example: The root names the craftsman, not the material.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指工匠，而不是材料。

items.meaning: relating to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns a field name into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把学科名词变成描述性形容词。

items.meaning: the study or process of crustal structure
items.meaningCN: 研究地壳结构的学科或过程
items.example: Plate tectonics united geology in the nineteen sixties.
items.exampleCN: 板块构造学说在二十世纪六十年代统一了地质学。

items.example: The basin is tectonically quiet today.
items.exampleCN: 这个盆地今天构造活动平静。

items.example: Ancient tectonism folded the layers twice.
items.exampleCN: 古老的构造作用两次使岩层褶皱。

items.meaningCN: 研究地壳变形的物理学
items.example: Tectonophysics models stress in the crust.
items.exampleCN: 构造物理学对地壳中的应力建模。

items.meaning: a rigid piece of the lithosphere
items.meaningCN: 岩石圈的一块刚性板块
items.example: Each tectonic plate moves as one body.
items.exampleCN: 每个构造板块作为整体移动。

items.meaning: raising of the crust by tectonic forces
items.meaningCN: 由构造力引起的地壳抬升
items.example: Tectonic uplift exposed marine fossils high in the mountains.
items.exampleCN: 构造抬升把海洋化石暴露在高山上。

items.meaning: an earthquake caused by fault slip
items.meaningCN: 由断层滑动引起的地震
items.example: The tectonic earthquake damaged several villages.
items.exampleCN: 这次构造地震损坏了几个村庄。

definition_zh: 构造地质学；地壳构造运动；建筑构造学
definition_en: the study of the structure and movement of the Earth's crust, or the art of construction
core_image: 一张大地构造图：岩层被压成褶皱、被拉成裂谷，整块地壳像被反复拆装的骨架
scene: 把裂谷两侧的地层对比之后，可以看出这片地形是怎样被塑造的。The map shows how tectonics has shaped the rift valley over millions of years.
sceneCN: 这里 tectonics 指「构造运动」（第 4 个义项：地壳的构造变形过程）；句意为这张图显示构造运动在数百万年间如何塑造了这条裂谷。

pos.zh: 构造地质学；构造运动；（建筑）构造学

senses.title: The study of crustal structure
senses.titleCN: 构造地质学：研究地壳结构的学科
senses.definition: the branch of geology that studies the structure and deformation of the Earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 研究地壳结构与变形的地质学分支
senses.example: She teaches tectonics at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学讲授构造地质学。
senses.why: A field name ending in -ics treats the subject as a body of knowledge, like physics or economics.
senses.whyCN: 以 -ics 结尾的学科名把研究对象当作一门知识体系，就像 physics 或 economics。

senses.title: Global plate tectonics
senses.definition: the theory and process by which lithospheric plates move and interact
senses.definitionCN: 岩石圈板块移动与相互作用的理论和过程
senses.example: Plate tectonics explains both earthquakes and mountain belts.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造学说同时解释了地震与山脉带。
senses.why: The global scale is the modern core of the field: one framework explains many separate phenomena.
senses.whyCN: 全球尺度是这门学科的现代核心：一个框架解释许多彼此分离的现象。

senses.title: Regional structure
senses.definition: the structural history of a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定区域的构造历史
senses.example: The tectonics of the basin record two episodes of rifting.
senses.exampleCN: 这个盆地的构造记录了两期裂谷作用。
senses.why: A region has its own stack of events, so the uncountable field name becomes countable in regional use.
senses.whyCN: 一个区域有自己的一串事件，因此这个不可数的学科名在区域用法中可以具体化。

senses.title: The process of deformation
senses.titleCN: 构造运动：地壳变形的过程
senses.definition: the actual deformation of the crust, such as folding, faulting and rifting
senses.definitionCN: 地壳实际发生的变形，如褶皱、断裂与裂谷作用
senses.example: The map shows how tectonics has shaped the rift valley over millions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图显示构造运动在数百万年间如何塑造了这条裂谷。
senses.why: The same noun can name the process rather than the study of the process, just as economics can mean the economy in action.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词可以指过程而不是对过程的研究，正如 economics 也可指实际运行的经济。

senses.title: The art of construction
senses.definition: in architecture, the discipline of how parts are joined and expressed
senses.definitionCN: 建筑学中研究构件如何拼接与表达的分支
senses.example: His book treats tectonics as the honesty of joints.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书把建筑构造学视为对接缝的诚实表达。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of the root: tekton is a builder, and tectonics is the art of building well.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根最古老的义项：tekton 是建造者，tectonics 就是好好建造的技艺。

senses.title: Structure on other planets
senses.definition: the study of crustal structure and deformation on other rocky bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究其他岩石天体地壳结构与变形的学科
senses.example: Planetary tectonics compares faults on Mars with those on Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 行星构造学把火星断层与地球断层作比较。
senses.why: The methods do not depend on the planet, only on whether a body has a brittle shell.
senses.whyCN: 这些方法不取决于哪颗行星，只取决于该天体是否拥有脆性外壳。

senses.title: A style of structural deformation
senses.titleCN: 构造样式：伸展、挤压等类型
senses.definition: a recognised style of deformation, such as extensional or compressional tectonics
senses.definitionCN: 被识别出的变形类型，如伸展构造或挤压构造
senses.example: Extensional tectonics produced a chain of parallel valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 伸展构造形成了一串平行的谷地。
senses.why: Geologists classify deformation by its geometry, so tectonics also names the style rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家按几何形态对变形分类，因此 tectonics 也指某种样式，而不是整个学科。

senses.title: A sequence of structural events
senses.definition: the ordered history of deformation events in a rock body
senses.definitionCN: 一个岩体内变形事件的有序历史
senses.example: The tectonics began with compression and ended with collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的构造演化以挤压开始，以塌陷结束。
senses.why: Structural history is a sequence, so the noun can name the order in which events happened.
senses.whyCN: 构造历史是一个序列，因此这个名词可以指事件发生的先后次序。

intro.en: Tectonics is the noun built on Greek tekton 'builder'. The same word names a science of the Earth and an art of building, two branches of one root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tectonics 是建立在希腊语 tekton「建造者」之上的名词。同一个词既指地球的科学，也指建造的艺术，是同一词根的两条分支。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek tekton 'builder' and tektonike (techne) 'the art of building' supply the root and the notion of a craft.
items.cn: 希腊语 tekton「建造者」与 tektonike (techne)「建造的艺术」提供了词根与「手艺」的概念。

items.en: Latin tectonicus supplied the adjective, and the noun tectonics was formed on the model of other -ics field names.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tectonicus 提供了形容词，名词 tectonics 则按其他 -ics 学科名的模式构成。

items.en: Geologists adopted tectonics for the study of folds, faults and the architecture of the crust.
items.cn: 地质学家采用 tectonics 指对褶皱、断层与地壳架构的研究。

items.en: Architectural writing kept the older craft sense, speaking of the tectonics of a building's joints.
items.cn: 建筑写作保留了更古老的工艺义，用 tectonics 指建筑接缝的构造。

items.en: Plate tectonics became the unifying theory of geology, and the plural-looking form now usually names the global process.
items.cn: 板块构造成为地质学的统一理论，这个看似复数的形式现在通常指全球尺度的过程。

items.en: The deeper history of tekein 'to build' is reconstructed, not attested; a widely cited proposal connects it with a root for weaving or fabricating.
items.cn: tekein「建造」的更早历史是重构而非有记录的；一个被广泛引用的假说把它连到表示编织或制作的词根上。

note.en: Group one separates tectonics from words that look or sound nearly identical; group two separates it from neighbouring Earth-science fields.
note.cn: 第一组把 tectonics 与看起来或听起来几乎相同的词分开；第二组把它与相邻的地球科学领域分开。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'relating to structure'; the noun tectonics names the field or the process.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「与构造有关的」形容词；名词 tectonics 指学科或过程。

entries.definition: the study or practice of a technique. It has the same opening but a different root vowel and a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 对某项技术的研究或实践。开头相同，但词根元音与含义都不同。

entries.definition: a strengthening medicine or a musical keynote. It lacks the tek- opening.
entries.definitionCN: 强壮剂，或音乐的主音。它没有 tek- 开头。

entries.definition: a planned move; the stressed vowel is /æ/, not /e/.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的行动；重读元音是 /æ/ 而不是 /e/。

entries.definition: the whole study of the Earth, including rocks, fossils and history; tectonics is one branch.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球的整体学科，包括岩石、化石与历史；tectonics 是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: the process of mountain formation; tectonics covers that and much more, including rifting.
entries.definitionCN: 造山过程；tectonics 覆盖的范围更广，也包括裂谷作用。

entries.definition: the physics of the Earth; it supplies the tools that tectonics uses.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球的物理学；它为构造研究提供工具。

entries.definition: an older word for crustal deformation, largely replaced by tectonics.
entries.definitionCN: 指地壳变形的旧术语，现多被 tectonics 取代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots and real neighbouring fields, so the word is anchored in the discipline rather than in a rhyme.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根与真实的相邻学科，因此这个词锚定在学科体系中，而不是靠押韵。

normal.en: tectonics is the noun, tectonic is the adjective, and -ics marks a field like physics or economics.
normal.cn: tectonics 是名词，tectonic 是形容词，-ics 像 physics、economics 一样标记一门学科。

normal.en: tekton means builder, so tectonics studies how the Earth is built and rebuilt.
normal.cn: tekton 表示建造者，所以 tectonics 研究地球如何被搭建与重建。

normal.en: Plate tectonics is the global theory; regional tectonics is its local application.
normal.cn: 板块构造是全球理论；区域构造是它在局部地区的应用。

normal.en: Extensional tectonics pulls the crust apart, compressional tectonics pushes it together.
normal.cn: 伸展构造把地壳拉开，挤压构造把地壳推挤到一起。

normal.en: Architects still use tectonics for the visible logic of joints, which keeps the builder root alive.
normal.cn: 建筑师仍用 tectonics 指接缝的可见逻辑，这使「建造者」词根保持活力。

abstract.en: Abstractly, tectonics is the grammar of assembly: which parts join, in what order, and how the joints show.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，tectonics 是组装语法：哪些部件相接、按什么次序、接缝如何显现。

abstract.en: The field and the craft share one idea: a structure is legible when its parts and joins can be read.
abstract.cn: 学科与手艺共享一个观念：当部件与接缝可读时，结构才是清晰的。

abstract.en: Symbol: a folded stack of layers with numbered events along its edge, showing a sequence of deformation.
abstract.cn: 符号：一叠褶皱的岩层，边缘标出编号事件，显示变形的先后序列。

examples.en: Plate tectonics became the central theory of modern geology.
examples.cn: 板块构造成为现代地质学的核心理论。

examples.en: The tectonics of the Andes records long-lived compression.
examples.cn: 安第斯山的构造记录了长期的挤压作用。

examples.en: She wrote a book on the tectonics of stone buildings.
examples.cn: 她写了一本关于石构建筑构造学的书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泰克托尼克斯」—— 木匠（tekton）的手艺变成一门学问 → tectonics 构造学

root: 源自希腊语 tekton（建造者）与 tektonike（建造的艺术），加 -ics 构成学科名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tectonics. The thread runs from a field of study to the process it studies, and back to the older craft of building.
sensesIntro.cn: tectonics 的八个义项。主线从一门学科延伸到它所研究的过程，再回到更古老的建造手艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the grammar of how a structure is assembled, whether crust or building.
core.cn: 核心意象：结构如何组装的语法，无论对象是地壳还是建筑。

branches.en: FIELD NAMES: a science of the Earth and a science of other rocky bodies.
branches.cn: 学科名称：关于地球的科学，以及关于其他岩石天体的科学。

branches.en: GLOBAL THEORY: plate tectonics unifies the field.
branches.cn: 全球理论：板块构造把这一领域统一起来。

branches.en: LOCAL HISTORY: a region and a rock body each have an ordered sequence of events.
branches.cn: 局部历史：一个区域和一个岩体都各自有一串有序事件。

branches.en: PROCESS AND STYLE: the noun names both the deformation and its recognised geometry.
branches.cn: 过程与样式：这个名词既指变形本身，也指被识别出的几何样式。

branches.en: CRAFT SENSE: architecture keeps the original art of joining parts.
branches.cn: 手艺义：建筑学保留了拼接构件这门最初的技艺。

intro.en: Tectonics is a root plus a field suffix, and that suffix is productive across the sciences.
intro.cn: tectonics 是一个词根加一个学科后缀，而这个后缀在各科学领域都能产。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek tekton and the noun-forming pattern -ics; scientific Latin passed the adjective tectonicus to English. No separate Latin root family exists here, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分是希腊语 tekton 与构成名词的 -ics 模式；科学拉丁语把形容词 tectonicus 传给英语。这里没有另一支拉丁词根族，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: The root names the maker of the frame.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指骨架的制造者。

items.structure: Greek-derived suffix for fields of study
items.meaning: a discipline or system of knowledge
items.example: Physics and economics use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: physics 与 economics 使用同一个后缀。

items.example: Tectonic forces fold the layers.
items.exampleCN: 构造力使岩层褶皱。

items.example: The margin is tectonically active.
items.exampleCN: 这个边缘构造活动活跃。

items.example: Tectonism folded the strata before the intrusion.
items.exampleCN: 在侵入体之前，构造作用已使地层褶皱。

items.meaningCN: 应用于地壳变形的物理学
items.example: Tectonophysics measures stress and strain.
items.exampleCN: 构造物理学测量应力与应变。

items.meaningCN: 研究与地震有关的构造的学科
items.example: Seismotectonics maps active faults.
items.exampleCN: 地震构造学测绘活动断层。

items.meaning: the theory of moving lithospheric plates
items.meaningCN: 岩石圈板块运动的理论
items.example: Plate tectonics replaced continental drift as the fuller theory.
items.exampleCN: 板块构造作为更完整的理论取代了大陆漂移说。

items.meaningCN: 由拉伸造成的构造变形
items.example: Extensional tectonics opened the basin.
items.exampleCN: 伸展构造把盆地拉开。

definition_zh: 板块构造学说；岩石圈板块运动与相互作用的全球理论
definition_en: the theory that the Earth's lithosphere is divided into plates that move and interact
core_image: 一只裂成多块硬壳的球，碎壳漂浮在软层上，彼此挤压、拉开、错动
scene: 地震为什么集中在环太平洋一带，并不是偶然。The theory of plate tectonics explains why earthquakes cluster along the Pacific rim.
sceneCN: 这里 plate tectonics 指「板块构造学说」（第 1 个义项：解释板块运动与相互作用的全球理论）；句意为板块构造学说解释了地震为何集中在环太平洋一带。

pos.zh: 板块构造（学说）；板块构造学

senses.title: The unifying theory
senses.titleCN: 板块构造学说：统一地质学的理论
senses.definition: the theory that the lithosphere is broken into plates that move over the weaker mantle
senses.definitionCN: 认为岩石圈裂成板块并在较软弱地幔之上运动的理论
senses.example: The theory of plate tectonics explains why earthquakes cluster along the Pacific rim.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造学说解释了地震为何集中在环太平洋一带。
senses.why: The name joins the object (plates) with the field (tectonics), so the phrase literally means the study of how plates are built and moved.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称把对象（板块）与学科（tectonics）合在一起，字面意思就是研究板块如何构成与运动。

senses.title: The process of plate motion
senses.definition: the actual movement and interaction of lithospheric plates
senses.definitionCN: 岩石圈板块实际的移动与相互作用
senses.example: Plate tectonics has been shaping this ocean basin for a hundred million years.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造作用塑造这个大洋盆地已有一亿年。
senses.why: Like tectonics alone, the phrase can name the process as well as the theory that describes it.
senses.whyCN: 与单用的 tectonics 一样，这个短语既可指过程，也可指描述过程的理论。

senses.title: A global framework
senses.definition: the global framework that links earthquakes, volcanoes, mountains and ocean basins
senses.definitionCN: 把地震、火山、山脉与大洋盆地联系起来的全球框架
senses.example: Plate tectonics turned separate observations into one connected story.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造把彼此分离的观察变成一个连贯的故事。
senses.why: The theory's power is unification: one mechanism at plate boundaries explains many surface features.
senses.whyCN: 这个理论的力量在于统一：板块边界上的一种机制解释了许多地表特征。

senses.title: Interaction at plate boundaries
senses.titleCN: 板块边界上的相互作用
senses.definition: the three ways plates meet: spreading, converging and sliding past each other
senses.definitionCN: 板块相接的三种方式：张裂、汇聚与错动
senses.example: Plate tectonics predicts different rock types at different boundary types.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造预言不同类型边界上会出现不同的岩石组合。
senses.why: Every boundary type has a characteristic geometry of stress, so the theory predicts what should form there.
senses.whyCN: 每种边界都有特征性的应力几何，因此理论可以预言那里应当形成什么。

senses.title: The reason for earthquake belts
senses.definition: the explanation of why earthquakes follow narrow belts rather than scattering evenly
senses.definitionCN: 解释地震为何沿狭窄条带分布而非均匀散布
senses.example: Plate tectonics showed that the Pacific ring of fire is a boundary, not a coincidence.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造说明环太平洋火山地震带是一条边界，而不是巧合。
senses.why: Friction and bending concentrate at plate edges, so strain accumulates there and releases as earthquakes.
senses.whyCN: 摩擦与弯折集中在板块边缘，应力在那里积累并以地震方式释放。

senses.title: The mechanism of mountains and rifts
senses.definition: the mechanism by which collisions raise mountains and extension opens rifts
senses.definitionCN: 碰撞抬升山脉、拉伸张开裂谷的机制
senses.example: Plate tectonics links the Himalaya to a collision and the Red Sea to a rift.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造把喜马拉雅山与一次碰撞、把红海与一条裂谷联系起来。
senses.why: Compression thickens the crust and extension thins it, so both mountain belts and rift valleys are boundary products.
senses.whyCN: 挤压使地壳增厚，拉伸使地壳变薄，因此山脉带与裂谷都是板块边界的产物。

senses.title: A tool for reconstructing the past
senses.definition: the use of plate motions to reconstruct the positions of ancient continents
senses.definitionCN: 用板块运动重建古大陆位置的方法
senses.example: Plate tectonics lets geologists place the continents on a map of two hundred million years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造使地质学家能画出两亿年前大陆的位置。
senses.why: If plates move at measurable rates, their past positions can be run backwards like a film.
senses.whyCN: 如果板块以可测量的速度移动，它们的过去位置就可以像倒放影片一样推算出来。

senses.title: Plate behaviour on other planets
senses.definition: the comparative study of whether other rocky planets have moving plates
senses.definitionCN: 比较研究其他岩石行星是否有运动板块
senses.example: Venus seems to lack plate tectonics, which changes how its heat escapes.
senses.exampleCN: 金星似乎没有板块构造，这改变了它散热的方式。
senses.why: A planet with plates cools differently from one with a single unbroken shell, so the comparison matters.
senses.whyCN: 有板块的行星与只有一整层外壳的行星散热方式不同，因此这种比较很重要。

intro.en: Plate tectonics is a twentieth-century compound of an everyday noun and a Greek-derived field name. Each part has its own history. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: plate tectonics 是二十世纪由日常名词与希腊来源的学科名构成的复合术语。两部分各有自己的历史。年代均为约数。

items.en: The plate element goes back through Old French plate 'thin metal sheet' to Medieval Latin plata and, generally accepted, to Greek platys 'broad, flat'.
items.cn: plate 一词经古法语 plate「薄金属片」上溯到中世纪拉丁语 plata，一般认为再追溯到希腊语 platys「宽而平的」。

items.en: The tectonics element comes from Greek tekton 'builder' and tektonikos 'relating to building'.
items.cn: tectonics 部分来自希腊语 tekton「建造者」与 tektonikos「与建造有关的」。

items.en: Alfred Wegener's continental drift proposed moving landmasses but lacked a convincing mechanism.
items.cn: 阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳的大陆漂移说提出陆块会移动，但缺少令人信服的机制。

items.en: Seafloor spreading supplied the mechanism, and the phrase plate tectonics was adopted for the theory of moving lithospheric plates.
items.cn: 海底扩张提供了机制，plate tectonics 这一说法被用来指岩石圈板块运动的理论。

items.en: The phrase is now the standard name of the unifying theory and is often shortened to tectonics in context.
items.cn: 这个短语现在是这一统一理论的标准名称，在语境中常简称为 tectonics。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its parts and near neighbours; group two separates it from other theories of the same generation.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与它的组成部分及形近词分开；第二组把它与同一时期的其他理论分开。

entries.definition: the field name alone; plate tectonics is the specific theory of moving plates.
entries.definitionCN: 单用的学科名；plate tectonics 特指板块运动的理论。

entries.definition: the adjective form used before a noun, as in plate tectonic processes.
entries.definitionCN: 作定语时的形容词形式，如 plate tectonic processes（板块构造过程）。

entries.definition: a small blood cell fragment; it shares plate but ends in the diminutive -let.
entries.definitionCN: 血液中的小块细胞碎片；它共享 plate，但结尾是表小的 -let。

entries.definition: a flat elevated area of land; it is a landform, not a theory.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的高地；它是地貌，不是理论。

entries.definition: the earlier idea that continents moved across the globe; it lacked a mechanism and was absorbed into plate tectonics.
entries.definitionCN: 早期认为大陆会在地球上移动的想法；它缺少机制，后来被板块构造吸收。

entries.definition: the process that creates new ocean floor at ridges; it supplied the mechanism plate tectonics needed.
entries.definitionCN: 在大洋中脊生成新洋底的过程；它为板块构造提供了所需机制。

entries.definition: the sinking of one plate beneath another; it is one part of plate tectonics, not the whole theory.
entries.definitionCN: 一个板块俯冲到另一个板块之下；它是板块构造的一部分，不是整个理论。

entries.definition: mountain building; it is a consequence of plate interaction, not the framework itself.
entries.definitionCN: 造山作用；它是板块相互作用的后果，而不是框架本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the phrase is readable part by part, and each part is a real word with a real history.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个短语可以逐部分读出，而每部分都是真实的词、有真实的历史。

normal.en: plate is the flat slab, tectonics is the building study: plate tectonics is the study of how flat slabs build the Earth's surface.
normal.cn: plate 是平板，tectonics 是建造之学：板块构造就是研究平板如何搭建地球表面。

normal.en: The theory has three boundary types: spreading, converging and sliding, which is why one framework covers so much.
normal.cn: 这个理论有三种边界：张裂、汇聚与错动，所以一个框架能覆盖很多现象。

normal.en: Continental drift was the proposal; seafloor spreading was the mechanism; plate tectonics was the full theory.
normal.cn: 大陆漂移是提法，海底扩张是机制，板块构造是完整的理论。

normal.en: The ring of fire is a plate boundary, which is why the phrase explains earthquake belts.
normal.cn: 环太平洋火山地震带是一条板块边界，所以这个短语能解释地震带。

normal.en: Plates move a few centimetres a year, about as fast as a fingernail grows.
normal.cn: 板块每年移动几厘米，大约和指甲生长一样快。

abstract.en: Abstractly, plate tectonics is a system of moving pieces: the whole surface is a puzzle whose pieces exchange material.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，板块构造是一个运动碎块的系统：整个表面是一幅拼图，碎块之间交换物质。

abstract.en: Its lesson is that large slow motion produces sudden events: centimeters per year become earthquakes in seconds.
abstract.cn: 它给出的启示是缓慢的大运动产生突发事件：每年几厘米的位移会在几秒内变成地震。

abstract.en: Symbol: a cracked shell with arrows pointing apart, together and sideways at three different seams.
abstract.cn: 符号：一层裂开的壳，三条不同的接缝上分别画着分开、合拢与侧向的箭头。

examples.en: Plate tectonics revolutionized geology in the nineteen sixties.
examples.cn: 板块构造学说在二十世纪六十年代彻底改变了地质学。

examples.en: The Alps formed through plate tectonics as two landmasses collided.
examples.cn: 阿尔卑斯山是两块陆地在板块构造作用下碰撞形成的。

examples.en: Without plate tectonics, the planet would lose heat in a very different way.
examples.cn: 如果没有板块构造，这颗行星散热的方式会大不相同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「平板 + 构造」—— 地球的硬壳像打碎的平板，一块块挪动 → plate tectonics 板块构造

root: plate 源自希腊语 platys（宽平的），tectonics 源自希腊语 tekton（建造者），合指「平板如何搭建地表」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of plate tectonics. The thread runs from the theory, to the process, to the boundaries, and out to other planets.
sensesIntro.cn: plate tectonics 的八个义项。主线从理论，到过程，到边界，再延伸到其他行星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cracked shell whose pieces move on a soft base.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层裂开的硬壳，碎块在软层上移动。

branches.en: THEORY: one framework unifies scattered surface features.
branches.cn: 理论：一个框架统一了散落的地表特征。

branches.en: PROCESS AND BOUNDARY: motion happens where plates meet, spread or slide.
branches.cn: 过程与边界：运动发生在板块相接、张裂或错动之处。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCES: strain at edges produces earthquakes, mountains and rifts.
branches.cn: 后果：边缘的应力产生地震、山脉与裂谷。

branches.en: TIME DEPTH: measurable motion can be run backwards to reconstruct the past.
branches.cn: 时间深度：可测量的运动可以倒推，用来重建过去。

branches.en: COMPARISON: the theory becomes a test of whether other planets have plates.
branches.cn: 比较：这个理论也成为检验其他行星是否有板块的标准。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Germanic-rooted everyday noun with a Greek-derived field name, and each part builds its own compounds.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个日常名词与一个希腊来源的学科名组合起来，两部分各自都能构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Plate reached English through Old French and Medieval Latin from Greek platys 'flat'; tectonics came through Latin tectonicus from Greek tekton 'builder'. The two halves have separate histories.
latinIntro.cn: plate 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语上溯到希腊语 platys「平的」；tectonics 经拉丁语 tectonicus 上溯到希腊语 tekton「建造者」。两半各有独立的历史。

items.structure: Greek platys 'flat' → Latin plata → Old French plate
items.example: The plate is a rigid slab of lithosphere.
items.exampleCN: 板块是岩石圈的一块刚性平板。

items.meaning: the study of structure and construction
items.meaningCN: 研究结构与建造的学科
items.example: Tectonics explains how the crust is assembled.
items.exampleCN: 构造学研究地壳如何组装。

items.meaning: the edge where two plates meet
items.example: Most volcanoes sit near a plate boundary.
items.exampleCN: 大多数火山位于板块边界附近。

items.example: Plate motion is measured by satellite signals.
items.exampleCN: 板块运动用卫星信号测量。

items.meaning: relating to the theory or its processes
items.meaningCN: 与板块构造理论或过程有关的
items.example: Plate-tectonic models predict where strain accumulates.
items.exampleCN: 板块构造模型预测应力在哪里积累。

items.meaning: another name for a plate boundary
items.meaningCN: 板块边界的另一种说法
items.example: The margin is the most active part of the plate.
items.exampleCN: 边缘是板块最活跃的部分。

items.meaning: a small plate within a larger system
items.example: A microplate rotates between two larger plates.
items.exampleCN: 一个小板块在两个较大板块之间旋转。

items.meaning: a minor plate below or within a larger one
items.meaningCN: 位于较大板块之下或内部的小板块
items.example: The subplate carries a small volcanic chain.
items.exampleCN: 这个小板块上带着一条小火山链。

definition_zh: 大陆的；大陆性的；欧洲大陆的；北美殖民地的
definition_en: relating to a continent, especially to the mainland of Europe or to continental climate
core_image: 一整块连成一片的陆地，与周围被海水隔开的岛屿形成对照
scene: 两大板块相撞之后，地壳被挤压得又厚又高。The collision built a high plateau where continental crust had thickened.
sceneCN: 这里 continental 指「大陆的」（第 1 个义项：与大陆地壳有关的）；句意为碰撞在陆壳增厚处抬升出一片高高原。

pos.zh: 大陆的；大陆性的；欧洲大陆的；（北美历史）大陆军的
（英式口语）欧洲大陆人

derivatives.zh: 大陆性（气候远离海洋的程度）

senses.title: Relating to a continent
senses.definition: relating to a continent or to the mainland rather than to islands
senses.definitionCN: 与大陆或本土有关的，而非与岛屿有关的
senses.example: The collision built a high plateau where continental crust had thickened.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞在陆壳增厚处抬升出一片高高原。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun continent to whatever it describes, so continental crust is the crust that belongs to a continent.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是把名词 continent 挂到所修饰的对象上，所以大陆地壳就是属于大陆的地壳。

senses.title: Mainland Europe
senses.definition: in British usage, relating to the mainland of Europe
senses.definitionCN: 在英式用法中，与欧洲大陆有关的
senses.example: They spent the summer travelling on the continental side of the Channel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夏天在海峡对岸的欧洲大陆旅行。
senses.why: From an island's viewpoint, 'the continent' is the nearest mainland, so continental means European in British speech.
senses.whyCN: 从岛屿的视角看，「大陆」就是最近的那块本土，所以英式口语中 continental 就指欧洲大陆的。

senses.title: Continental climate
senses.definition: describing a climate with hot summers and cold winters far from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 描述远离海洋、夏热冬冷的气候
senses.example: Continental interiors swing from hot summers to freezing winters.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆内部从炎夏摆到严寒的冬天。
senses.why: Land heats and cools faster than water, so places far inside a continent have a wider yearly range.
senses.whyCN: 陆地比水体升温降温更快，所以深入大陆内部的地区年温差更大。

senses.title: Relating to the continental shelf
senses.definition: describing the shallow sea floor that extends from a coast
senses.definitionCN: 描述从海岸延伸出去的浅海底
senses.example: Continental shelf waters support most of the world's fisheries.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆架水域支撑着世界大部分的渔业。
senses.why: The shelf is submerged continental crust, so the adjective marks it as part of the continent rather than the deep ocean.
senses.whyCN: 大陆架是被海水淹没的大陆地壳，因此这个形容词标明它属于大陆而不是深海。

senses.title: The American colonial sense
senses.definition: relating to the American colonies, as in the Continental Army
senses.definitionCN: 与美国殖民地有关的，如大陆军
senses.example: The Continental Congress met in Philadelphia.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆会议在费城召开。
senses.why: The colonies called the shared landmass 'the continent', so their army and congress took the name.
senses.whyCN: 各殖民地把自己所在的共同陆地称为「大陆」，因此他们的大陆军与大陆会议就用了这个名字。

senses.title: Relating to continental plates
senses.definition: describing the thick, buoyant parts of the crust that carry land
senses.definitionCN: 描述承载陆地、厚而轻的地壳部分
senses.example: Continental lithosphere floats higher than oceanic lithosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆岩石圈比大洋岩石圈浮得更高。
senses.why: Continental crust is less dense, so it rides high and cannot easily be subducted.
senses.whyCN: 大陆地壳密度较小，因此浮得高，也不容易被俯冲带走。

senses.title: Continental style
senses.definition: describing European habits of food, dress or daily life
senses.definitionCN: 描述欧洲的饮食、穿着或日常习惯
senses.example: The cafe serves a continental breakfast of bread and coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆供应面包配咖啡的欧陆式早餐。
senses.why: The label marks a style as coming from the mainland rather than from British practice.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签标明某种风格来自欧洲大陆，而不是英国本土的做法。

senses.title: Relating to continental law
senses.definition: describing the European legal tradition based on written codes
senses.definitionCN: 描述以成文法典为基础的欧洲法律传统
senses.example: Continental law relies on written codes more than on case precedent.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆法系更依赖成文法典，而不是判例。
senses.why: Legal systems differ by region, so continental marks the code-based tradition of mainland Europe.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系按地区不同，因此 continental 标记欧洲大陆以法典为基础的传统。

intro.en: Continental is the adjective of continent, from Latin continens 'holding together'. The word began as a description of continuous land and later acquired political and climatic senses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: continental 是 continent 的形容词，源自拉丁语 continens「连在一起」。这个词最初描述连续的陆地，后来获得政治与气候义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Continens is the present participle of continere 'to hold together, contain', built from com- 'together' plus tenere 'to hold'.
items.cn: continens 是 continere「连在一起、容纳」的现在分词，由 com-「共同」加 tenere「握住」构成。

items.en: Terra continens meant 'continuous land', land not broken by sea, which is how the noun continent began.
items.cn: terra continens 意为「连续的陆地」，即未被海水分隔的陆地，名词 continent 就是由此而来。

items.en: Old French continental and English continental kept the sense 'belonging to a continent', first as a geographic description.
items.cn: 古法语 continental 与英语 continental 保留了「属于大陆的」这一义，最初是地理描述。

items.en: British speakers narrowed 'the Continent' to mainland Europe, so continental gained the sense 'European'.
items.cn: 英式使用者把 the Continent 缩小为欧洲大陆，于是 continental 获得了「欧洲的」这一义。

items.en: The American colonies used continental for their shared landmass, producing the Continental Congress and Continental Army.
items.cn: 北美殖民地用 continental 指他们共同的陆地，于是有了大陆会议与大陆军。

items.en: Geology added continental crust, continental shelf and continental drift, all built on the same 'continuous land' idea.
items.cn: 地质学增加了大陆地壳、大陆架与大陆漂移等说法，全部建立在同一个「连续陆地」观念上。

note.en: Group one holds words whose spelling or sound is close to continental; group two holds adjectives that also describe land on a large scale.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音接近 continental 的词；第二组是同样描述大尺度陆地的形容词。

entries.definition: the noun meaning a large landmass; continental is its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 表示大块陆地的名词；continental 是它的形容词。

entries.definition: happening repeatedly over time; it comes from continue, not from continent.
entries.definitionCN: 在时间上反复发生的；它来自 continue，而不是 continent。

entries.definition: going on without a break; it describes time or space, not a landmass.
entries.definitionCN: 不中断地持续；它描述时间或空间，不描述陆地。

entries.definition: touching along a border; it describes adjacency, not a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 沿边界相接的；它描述相邻关系，不指大陆。

entries.definition: the main land area of a country or region, as opposed to its islands.
entries.definitionCN: 一国或一地区的主要陆地区域，相对于其岛屿而言。

entries.definition: away from the coast; it describes position, not political or climatic style.
entries.definitionCN: 远离海岸的；它描述位置，而非政治或气候风格。

entries.definition: relating to Europe; it covers the British sense of continental but not the geological ones.
entries.definitionCN: 与欧洲有关的；它覆盖 continental 的英式义，但不覆盖地质义。

entries.definition: a very large continuous area of land; it is the thing continental describes.
entries.definitionCN: 极大的一片连续陆地；它是 continental 所描述的对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real derivatives and real geographic contrasts, so the adjective is tied to the noun it modifies.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的派生词与真实的地理对照，因此这个形容词紧扣它所修饰的名词。

normal.en: continental is just continent plus -al: the adjective adds 'relating to' to the noun.
normal.cn: continental 就是 continent 加 -al：形容词给名词加上「与……有关」的意思。

normal.en: Continental crust is thick and light, which is why continents ride high above the ocean floor.
normal.cn: 大陆地壳又厚又轻，所以大陆高高地浮在洋底之上。

normal.en: A continental climate is one far from the sea, with hot summers and cold winters.
normal.cn: 大陆性气候就是远离海洋、夏热冬冷的气候。

normal.en: In British English, continental often just means European, as in a continental breakfast.
normal.cn: 在英式英语中，continental 常常就指欧洲的，比如欧陆式早餐。

normal.en: The Continental Congress took its name from the shared North American landmass.
normal.cn: 大陆会议的名字来自北美各殖民地共享的那块陆地。

abstract.en: Abstractly, continental means 'belonging to the big continuous block', as opposed to the fragment or the island.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，continental 表示「属于连成一片的大块」，与碎片或岛屿相对。

abstract.en: The word always measures scale: what counts as the mainland depends on where the speaker stands.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终在衡量尺度：什么算「大陆」，取决于说话人站在哪里。

abstract.en: Symbol: one large continuous shape and three small detached dots beside it.
abstract.cn: 符号：一个连成一片的大块，旁边三个分离的小点。

examples.en: Continental crust is older and thicker than oceanic crust.
examples.cn: 大陆地壳比大洋地壳更古老、更厚。

examples.en: The interior has a harsh continental climate.
examples.cn: 内陆地区是严酷的大陆性气候。

examples.en: They took a train across continental Europe.
examples.cn: 他们乘火车穿越欧洲大陆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康提南头」—— 一块连成一片的大陆地伸到南头 → continental 大陆的

root: 源自拉丁语 continens（连在一起的陆地），由 com-（共同）加 tenere（握住）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of continental. They all point to one large continuous landmass, whether the context is geology, climate, Europe or American history.
sensesIntro.cn: continental 的八个义项都指向同一块连成一片的大陆地，无论语境是地质、气候、欧洲还是美国历史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one large continuous land block, opposed to islands and fragments.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块连成一片的大陆地，与岛屿和碎片相对。

branches.en: LAND AND SHELF: the same continent continues under shallow sea.
branches.cn: 陆地与陆架：同一块大陆在浅海之下继续延伸。

branches.en: MAINLAND STYLE: from an island, the mainland means Europe in food, habit and law.
branches.cn: 大陆风格：从岛屿看，大陆在饮食、习惯与法律上都指欧洲。

branches.en: CLIMATE: distance from the sea makes the yearly range wider.
branches.cn: 气候：离海越远，年温差越大。

branches.en: CRUST: thick light rock makes continents float high.
branches.cn: 地壳：厚而轻的岩石使大陆浮得高。

branches.en: HISTORY: the colonies named their shared land the continent.
branches.cn: 历史：各殖民地把自己共享的陆地称为大陆。

intro.en: Continental is the adjective built on continent with -al, and the same pattern produces several compounds about crossing or belonging to continents.
intro.cn: continental 是由 continent 加 -al 构成的形容词，同一模式还产生若干表示「跨越大陆」或「属于次大陆」的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is continere 'to hold together' (com- + tenere); continens and the adjective continentalis pass into English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 continere「连在一起」（com- + tenere）；continens 与形容词 continentalis 经法语进入英语。

items.example: The Latin verb supplies the 'continuous' idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词提供了「连续」的意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The continent stretches from ocean to ocean.
items.exampleCN: 这块大陆从一个大洋延伸到另一个大洋。

items.example: The climate is continentally dry.
items.exampleCN: 这里的气候具有大陆性的干燥。
