items.meaning: the degree to which a place is far from the sea
items.meaningCN: 某地远离海洋的程度（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: Continentality raises the summer temperature.
items.exampleCN: 大陆性提高了夏季温度。

items.example: Intercontinental missiles cross oceans.
items.exampleCN: 洲际导弹跨越海洋。

items.example: A transcontinental railway linked the two coasts.
items.exampleCN: 一条横贯大陆的铁路连接了两岸。

items.example: The subcontinental shelf is unusually wide.
items.exampleCN: 这个次大陆的陆架异常宽阔。

items.meaning: the shallow sea floor next to a continent
items.example: The continental shelf is rich in fish.
items.exampleCN: 大陆架鱼类丰富。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 连在一起的；连续的陆地

definition_zh: 大陆，洲；欧洲大陆；（形容词）有自制力的
definition_en: one of the large landmasses of the world; also an adjective meaning self-controlled
core_image: 一块被海洋围住、连成一片的巨大陆地，与四周零散的岛屿分开
scene: 世界地图上，非洲的面积排在第二位。Africa is the second largest continent by land area.
sceneCN: 这里 continent 指「大洲」（第 1 个义项：世界上的大块陆地之一）；句意为按陆地面积计算，非洲是第二大的洲。

pos.zh: 大陆；洲；（英式）欧洲大陆
有自制力的；能控制大小便的

senses.title: One of the great landmasses
senses.titleCN: 大洲：世界上的大块陆地之一
senses.definition: one of the large continuous landmasses of the world, such as Africa or Asia
senses.definitionCN: 世界上的大块连续陆地之一，如非洲或亚洲
senses.example: Africa is the second largest continent by land area.
senses.exampleCN: 按陆地面积计算，非洲是第二大的洲。
senses.why: The Latin source meant 'continuous land', so a continent is land that holds together as one mass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「连续的陆地」，所以 continent 就是连成一整块的土地。

senses.title: A continuous landmass
senses.definition: a body of land not broken up by sea, as opposed to an island
senses.definitionCN: 未被海水分隔的大片陆地，与岛屿相对
senses.example: The bridge connects the island to the continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥把岛屿与大陆连接起来。
senses.why: The oldest sense is about continuity: land is a continent when you can walk across it without crossing water.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项关乎连续性：能不用跨水就走过去的大片土地才叫大陆。

senses.title: Mainland Europe
senses.titleCN: 欧洲大陆（英式 the Continent）
senses.definition: in British English, the mainland of Europe
senses.definitionCN: 在英式英语中，指欧洲大陆
senses.example: They crossed to the Continent for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夏天渡海去了欧洲大陆。
senses.why: A British speaker on an island naturally calls the nearest mainland 'the continent'.
senses.whyCN: 身处岛屿的英国人自然会称最近的那块本土为「大陆」。

senses.title: Dry land as opposed to sea
senses.definition: land as a whole, seen in contrast with the oceans
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的陆地，与海洋相对
senses.example: Life moved from the sea onto the continent long ago.
senses.exampleCN: 生命很久以前从海洋登上了陆地。
senses.why: This use treats the whole land surface as one mass, which is the same 'continuous land' idea at a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 这种用法把整个陆地表面视为一整块，是「连续陆地」观念在更大尺度上的延伸。

senses.title: Self-controlled
senses.definition: able to control one's desires or bodily functions
senses.definitionCN: 能控制自己的欲望或身体机能的
senses.example: The patient remained continent after the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗之后病人能够控制排泄。
senses.why: This is a separate adjective from Latin continens 'holding oneself in', so it means self-restraint rather than land.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个独立的形容词，来自拉丁语 continens「把自己收住」，所以它指自我克制而非陆地。

senses.title: A continent in geology
senses.definition: a region of thick continental crust, including its submerged shelf
senses.definitionCN: 由厚大陆地壳构成的区域，包括被淹没的陆架
senses.example: Geologists define a continent by its crust, not by its coastline.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家按地壳而不是海岸线来界定大陆。
senses.why: The geological unit includes the shelf because the same thick crust continues under shallow water.
senses.whyCN: 地质单位包括陆架，因为同一片厚地壳在浅海之下继续延伸。

senses.title: An ancient continent
senses.definition: a landmass of the geological past, now fragments of several modern continents
senses.definitionCN: 地质历史上的陆块，如今是几个现代大陆的碎块
senses.example: The ancient continent split into pieces that drifted apart.
senses.exampleCN: 这块古大陆裂成碎块，漂移分开。
senses.why: Reconstruction treats today's continents as pieces of older ones, so the noun is used for past landmasses.
senses.whyCN: 重建工作把今天的大陆视为更古老陆块的碎片，因此这个名词也用于过去的陆块。

senses.title: A cultural or political region
senses.titleCN: 文化或政治意义上的大陆
senses.definition: a large region treated as a unit in culture, politics or trade
senses.definitionCN: 在文化、政治或贸易中被当作一个整体的大区域
senses.example: The treaty covers the whole continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约覆盖整个大陆。
senses.why: Once a landmass is named, it can also stand for the societies on it, so continent can mean a political region.
senses.whyCN: 一块陆地一旦被命名，也可以代表其上的社会，因此 continent 可指一个政治区域。

intro.en: Continent comes from Latin terra continens 'continuous land'. The land sense and the self-control sense come from the same verb but developed separately. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: continent 来自拉丁语 terra continens「连续的陆地」。陆地义与自制义出自同一个动词，但各自独立发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Continere 'to hold together, keep in' is com- 'together' plus tenere 'to hold'. Its participle continens means both 'continuous' and 'holding oneself in'.
items.cn: continere「连在一起、收住」由 com-「共同」加 tenere「握住」构成。其分词 continens 同时有「连续的」与「自我克制」两义。

items.en: Terra continens was land that holds together, as opposed to islands or separated regions.
items.cn: terra continens 指连成一片的陆地，与岛屿或分离的区域相对。

items.en: Old French continent and Middle English continent kept the geographic sense and gradually narrowed it to the great landmasses.
items.cn: 古法语 continent 与中古英语 continent 保留了地理义，并逐渐收窄为几块大洲。

items.en: British speakers shortened 'the continent of Europe' to 'the Continent', which is why continental can mean European.
items.cn: 英式使用者把「欧洲大陆」缩为 the Continent，这就是 continental 可指欧洲的原因。

items.en: The adjective meaning 'self-controlled' comes from the same participle but followed a medical path, giving continence and incontinent.
items.cn: 表示「有自制力」的形容词同出这一分词，但走的是医学路径，产生了 continence 与 incontinent。

items.en: Geology added supercontinent and subcontinent and redefined a continent by its crust, not by its outline on a map.
items.cn: 地质学增加了超大陆与次大陆等说法，并按地壳而非地图轮廓重新界定大陆。

note.en: Group one holds words that look and sound like continent; group two holds the geographic terms that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形音接近 continent 的词；第二组是语义上与之重叠的地理术语。

entries.definition: the adjective of continent, ending in -al; continent itself is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: continent 的形容词，以 -al 结尾；continent 本身是名词。

entries.definition: self-restraint, especially control of bodily functions; it comes from the adjective sense, not the land sense.
entries.definitionCN: 自我克制，尤指对排泄的控制；它来自形容词义，而非陆地义。

entries.definition: repeated again and again; it belongs to continue, not to continent.
entries.definitionCN: 一次又一次地重复；它属于 continue，不属于 continent。

entries.definition: what is inside something, or satisfied; it shares the opening but has a different ending and history.
entries.definitionCN: 内容，或满足的；开头相同，但结尾与历史不同。

entries.definition: any very large continuous area of land; it avoids the political and cultural freight of continent.
entries.definitionCN: 任何极大的连续陆地区域；它避开 continent 的政治与文化含义。

entries.definition: the main land of a country, seen in contrast with its islands; the contrast is local, not global.
entries.definitionCN: 一国的主要陆地，相对于其岛屿；这种对照是局部的，不是全球的。

entries.definition: a huge landmass formed when several continents join together.
entries.definitionCN: 几个大陆拼合而成的巨大陆块。

entries.definition: a very large region that is part of a continent but treated separately, such as India.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某个大陆但被单独看待的极大区域，如印度次大陆。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real geographic labels, so the two senses can be kept apart by their histories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件与真实的地理名称，因此两个义项可以靠历史分开。

normal.en: continere means hold together, so a continent is land that holds together as one piece.
normal.cn: continere 表示连在一起，所以 continent 就是连成一整块的陆地。

normal.en: The land sense and the self-control sense share a participle but split early: one became geography, the other medicine.
normal.cn: 陆地义与自制义共享一个分词，但很早分开：一个走向地理，一个走向医学。

normal.en: In British English, 'the Continent' is specifically Europe, which is why continental breakfast means European-style breakfast.
normal.cn: 在英式英语中，the Continent 特指欧洲，所以 continental breakfast 指欧陆式早餐。

normal.en: A supercontinent is many continents joined; a subcontinent is one large piece of a continent.
normal.cn: 超大陆是许多大陆拼在一起；次大陆是一个大陆中的一大块。

normal.en: Geologists include the shelf, because the same thick crust continues under shallow water.
normal.cn: 地质学家把陆架算进去，因为同一片厚地壳在浅海之下继续延伸。

abstract.en: Abstractly, continent means a whole that holds together: the opposite of a scattered archipelago.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，continent 表示连成整体的一个大块，与零散群岛相反。

abstract.en: The word is always relative: a continent on a world map can be a mainland when seen from an island.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终是相对的：世界地图上的一个洲，从岛屿看就成了本土。

abstract.en: Symbol: a large closed shape surrounded by a dotted ring of small separate shapes.
abstract.cn: 符号：一个闭合的大块，外面一圈小点是分离的岛屿。

examples.en: Seven continents cover about thirty percent of the Earth's surface.
examples.cn: 七大洲覆盖地球表面约百分之三十。

examples.en: The ancient continent later split into two landmasses.
examples.cn: 这块古大陆后来裂成两块陆地。

examples.en: The training helped the patient stay continent at night.
examples.cn: 这项训练帮助病人夜间保持控尿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康提南」—— 一块大陆连成一片，像被提起来放在南边 → continent 大陆、洲

root: 源自拉丁语 continere（连在一起）的现在分词 continens，字面义为「连续的陆地」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of continent. Most describe a continuous landmass; one separate adjective describes self-control, and one use names a past landmass.
sensesIntro.cn: continent 的八个义项。多数描述连成一片的陆地；有一个独立的形容词义表示自制，还有一个义项指过去的陆块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: land that holds together, seen against islands and sea.
core.cn: 核心意象：连成一片的陆地，以岛屿与海洋为对照。

branches.en: THE SAME MASS: a named continent and a continuous landmass are one idea at two scales.
branches.cn: 同一整体：被命名的大洲与连成一片的陆地是同一观念在两个尺度上。

branches.en: MAINLAND AS A UNIT: Europe and other regions become 'the continent' for those nearby.
branches.cn: 作为单位的大陆：对附近的人来说，欧洲等区域就成了「大陆」。

branches.en: LAND VERSUS SEA: the whole land surface, and the crustal unit that includes the shelf.
branches.cn: 陆与海：整个陆地表面，以及包含陆架的地壳单位。

branches.en: PAST MASSES: reconstruction turns today's continents into fragments of older ones.
branches.cn: 过去的陆块：重建把今天的大陆变成更古老陆块的碎片。

branches.en: SEPARATE ADJECTIVE: holding oneself in gives self-control, not geography.
branches.cn: 独立的形容词：把自己收住产生自制义，与地理无关。

intro.en: Continent builds a compact family: an adjective, an abstract noun, a negative adjective and two prefixes for joined or partial landmasses.
intro.cn: continent 构成一个紧凑的词族：一个形容词、一个抽象名词、一个否定形容词，以及两个表示拼合或部分陆块的前缀词。

latinIntro.en: Latin continere 'to hold together' supplies continens; the same root gives continence and incontinent, while continentalis supplies the geographic adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 continere「连在一起」提供 continens；同一词根产生 continence 与 incontinent，而 continentalis 提供地理形容词。

items.example: The verb carries both the land and the restraint ideas.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时承载陆地与克制两种意思。

items.example: Continental crust is thick and light.
items.exampleCN: 大陆地壳厚而轻。

items.meaning: self-restraint, especially control of the body
items.meaningCN: 自制，尤指对身体的控制
items.example: Continence improved after the therapy.
items.exampleCN: 治疗后控尿能力有所改善。

items.meaning: unable to control the body; lacking restraint
items.example: The injury left him incontinent.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤使他失禁。

items.meaning: a landmass formed by several continents joining
items.meaningCN: 由几个大陆拼合而成的巨大陆块
items.example: Pangaea was a supercontinent.
items.exampleCN: 泛大陆曾是一块超大陆。

items.meaning: a large region treated as a unit within a continent
items.meaningCN: 大陆内部被单独看待的大区域
items.example: The Indian subcontinent has its own monsoon.
items.exampleCN: 印度次大陆有自己的季风。

items.meaning: a small fragment of continental crust
items.example: A microcontinent can be stranded in an ocean.
items.exampleCN: 小陆块可能被困在大洋中间。

items.meaning: a continent of an earlier geological age
items.example: Paleocontinent maps show how the pieces once fitted.
items.exampleCN: 古大陆图显示这些碎块当初如何拼合。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 连续的陆地；连在一起的

definition_zh: 大陆漂移；大陆块在地球表面相对移动的假说
definition_en: the idea that the continents have moved slowly across the Earth's surface over geological time
core_image: 几块大陆像浮冰一样在地球表面缓慢漂开，彼此之间的海岸线曾经拼得严丝合缝
scene: 相隔大洋的两岸竟然发现了同一种古老蕨类的化石。Fossils of the same fern occur on landmasses now separated by an ocean, evidence for continental drift.
sceneCN: 这里 continental drift 指「大陆漂移」（第 1 个义项：大陆块在地表相对移动的假说）；句意为同一种古老蕨类的化石出现在如今被大洋隔开的陆块上，这成为大陆漂移的证据。

pos.zh: 大陆漂移（说）；大陆块的水平移动

senses.title: The hypothesis of moving continents
senses.titleCN: 大陆漂移说：大陆会移动的假说
senses.definition: the hypothesis that continents have moved slowly across the globe over geological time
senses.definitionCN: 认为大陆在地质时间里缓慢移动的假说
senses.example: Fossils of the same fern occur on landmasses now separated by an ocean, evidence for continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 同一种古老蕨类的化石出现在如今被大洋隔开的陆块上，这成为大陆漂移的证据。
senses.why: The phrase names the motion directly: continental tells us what moves, drift tells us how slowly and freely.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语直接命名运动：continental 说明移动的是什么，drift 说明移动得缓慢而自由。

senses.title: The motion itself
senses.definition: the actual relative motion of continents over the Earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 大陆在地球表面实际的相对运动
senses.example: Continental drift continues today at a few centimetres a year.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆漂移今天仍在继续，每年几厘米。
senses.why: Like most theory names, the phrase can denote the process as well as the idea about it.
senses.whyCN: 像多数理论名称一样，这个短语既可指过程，也可指关于过程的想法。

senses.title: Wegener's proposal
senses.definition: the specific early-twentieth-century proposal of Alfred Wegener
senses.definitionCN: 阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳在二十世纪初提出的具体假说
senses.example: Wegener's continental drift was rejected at first for lacking a mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 魏格纳的大陆漂移说最初因缺少机制而被否定。
senses.why: The phrase is historically tied to one proposal, so it can name that proposal rather than the general process.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语在历史上与一个具体提案绑定，因此可指那个提案而非一般过程。

senses.title: The evidence from matching coasts
senses.definition: the evidence that coastlines and rock sequences on opposite sides of an ocean match
senses.definitionCN: 大洋两岸的海岸线与岩层序列能够对上的证据
senses.example: The matching coastlines of South America and Africa were early support for continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 南美与非洲海岸线的吻合是大陆漂移说的早期支持。
senses.why: If two shores fit like puzzle pieces, the simplest reading is that they were once one piece.
senses.whyCN: 如果两岸像拼图一样吻合，最简单的解释就是它们曾经是一块。

senses.title: The fossil evidence
senses.definition: the evidence that identical fossils occur on continents now far apart
senses.definitionCN: 相同化石出现在如今天各一方的不同大陆上的证据
senses.example: Glossopteris fossils were a key clue for continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 舌羊齿化石是大陆漂移说的关键线索。
senses.why: A plant that cannot cross an ocean should not appear on both sides unless the land was once joined.
senses.whyCN: 一种无法跨洋传播的植物不该出现在两岸，除非那片陆地曾经相连。

senses.title: The missing mechanism
senses.definition: the weakness of the early theory, which could not explain what moved the continents
senses.definitionCN: 早期理论的弱点：无法解释是什么推动了大陆
senses.example: Continental drift stalled until seafloor spreading supplied a mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆漂移说停滞不前，直到海底扩张提供了机制。
senses.why: A theory that describes motion without a driver is incomplete, which is why the phrase is often paired with 'hypothesis'.
senses.whyCN: 只描述运动而不给出驱动力的理论是不完整的，因此这个短语常与「假说」搭配。

senses.title: The ancestor of plate tectonics
senses.definition: the earlier framework that plate tectonics later absorbed and explained
senses.definitionCN: 后来被板块构造吸收并解释的早期框架
senses.example: Plate tectonics grew out of continental drift and seafloor spreading.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造由大陆漂移与海底扩张发展而来。
senses.why: The old idea supplied the observation; the new theory supplied the machinery, so the two are ancestor and descendant.
senses.whyCN: 旧想法提供了观察，新理论提供了机制，因此两者是前身与后继的关系。

senses.title: A metaphor for slow separation
senses.titleCN: 比喻：缓慢而巨大的分离
senses.definition: used figuratively for things that separate slowly and irreversibly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻缓慢而不可逆地分开的事物
senses.example: The two departments underwent a kind of continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个部门经历了一种缓慢的分离。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the pace of the process: almost invisible day by day, enormous over time.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了过程的节奏：逐日几乎看不见，长期却极其巨大。

intro.en: Continental drift is a modern scientific phrase. Its two words are ordinary English, but the idea was assembled from geology, fossils and coastlines in the early twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: continental drift 是现代科学短语。两个词都是普通英语词，但其观念是二十世纪初从地质、化石与海岸线证据中组装起来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Continental comes from Latin continere 'to hold together'; drift comes from Old English drifan 'to drive, be driven', which later gave the sense of being carried by currents.
items.cn: continental 来自拉丁语 continere「连在一起」；drift 来自古英语 drifan「驱动、被推动」，后来产生「被水流带走」的意思。

items.en: Drift first meant driving or being driven; the modern sense of slow, passive movement developed in the context of ships, snow and currents.
items.cn: drift 最初指驱动或被驱动；现代「缓慢被动移动」义是在船只、雪与洋流的语境中发展出来的。

items.en: Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined and later moved apart, supported by matching coasts, fossils and rock belts.
items.cn: 阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳提出大陆曾经相连、后来分开，并用海岸吻合、化石与岩带作为证据。

items.en: The idea was widely resisted because no known force could move continents through the ocean floor.
items.cn: 这个想法长期遭到抵制，因为当时不知道有什么力量能让大陆穿过洋底移动。

items.en: Seafloor spreading and plate tectonics supplied the mechanism, and continental drift was absorbed as part of the larger theory.
items.cn: 海底扩张与板块构造提供了机制，大陆漂移被吸收为更大理论的一部分。

items.en: The phrase survives as the historical name of the early hypothesis and as a general label for the relative motion of continents.
items.cn: 这个短语作为早期假说的历史名称保留下来，也用作大陆相对运动的通称。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from look-alike and sound-alike words; group two separates it from the theories and processes it is often mixed with.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与形近、音近词分开；第二组把它与常被混淆的理论和过程分开。

entries.definition: a first version of a text, or a plan; it is spelled with -a and has nothing to do with moving land.
entries.definitionCN: 文本的初稿或计划；拼写用 -a，与陆地移动无关。

entries.definition: the noun or verb meaning slow passive movement; continental drift adds the object that moves.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缓慢被动移动的名词或动词；continental drift 加上了移动的对象。

entries.definition: floating without control; the prefix a- adds the sense of being loose.
entries.definitionCN: 失去控制地漂浮；前缀 a- 增添了「松脱」的意思。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'relating to a continent'; alone it does not imply any theory.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「与大陆有关的」形容词；单独使用时不含任何理论含义。

entries.definition: the fuller theory of moving lithospheric plates that explained and replaced continental drift.
entries.definitionCN: 解释并取代大陆漂移说的、关于岩石圈板块运动的更完整理论。

entries.definition: the creation of new ocean floor at ridges; it provided the mechanism continental drift lacked.
entries.definitionCN: 在大洋中脊生成新洋底；它为大陆漂移说提供了所缺的机制。

entries.definition: the apparent movement of the poles relative to a continent; it is not the same as continents moving apart.
entries.definitionCN: 极相对于大陆的视移动；这与大陆彼此分开不同。

entries.definition: movement from one place to another, usually by people or animals; it lacks the geological scale.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物从一个地方到另一个地方的移动；它没有地质尺度的含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real evidence types and real historical sequence, so the phrase is remembered as a story rather than a slogan.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的证据类型与真实的历史顺序，因此这个短语作为一段故事被记住，而不是口号。

normal.en: The phrase says exactly what it means: continents drift, slowly and passively, like rafts on a current.
normal.cn: 这个短语说的就是字面意思：大陆漂移，缓慢而被动，像水流上的筏子。

normal.en: The three classic clues are matching coastlines, matching fossils and matching rock belts.
normal.cn: 三条经典证据是海岸线吻合、化石吻合与岩带吻合。

normal.en: Wegener proposed the drift; seafloor spreading explained it; plate tectonics replaced it with a fuller framework.
normal.cn: 魏格纳提出漂移，海底扩张解释漂移，板块构造以更完整的框架取代它。

normal.en: The old theory's weakness was the missing mechanism, not the evidence.
normal.cn: 旧理论的弱点是缺少机制，而不是缺少证据。

normal.en: Continents move about as fast as a fingernail grows, which is why the drift is invisible in a lifetime.
normal.cn: 大陆移动的速度大约和指甲生长一样快，所以在一生之中看不见这种漂移。

abstract.en: Abstractly, continental drift is separation without a visible cause: pieces move apart so slowly that each day looks unchanged.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，大陆漂移是没有可见原因的分离：碎块移动得如此缓慢，以至于每一天看起来都没变。

abstract.en: Its lesson is that a correct observation can wait decades for the right mechanism.
abstract.cn: 它给出的启示是：一个正确的观察可能等待数十年才等到合适的机制。

abstract.en: Symbol: two puzzle pieces that once fitted, now separated by a widening gap with small arrows.
abstract.cn: 符号：两块曾经吻合的拼图，如今被一条不断变宽的缝隙分开，缝中有小箭头。

examples.en: Continental drift explained why similar fossils appear on distant continents.
examples.cn: 大陆漂移说解释了为什么相似化石出现在相距遥远的大陆上。

examples.en: The idea of continental drift was debated for decades before plate tectonics.
examples.cn: 在板块构造出现之前，大陆漂移的想法被争论了几十年。

examples.en: Modern measurements confirm continental drift at a few centimetres per year.
examples.cn: 现代测量证实大陆漂移的速度是每年几厘米。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「大陆 + 漂移」—— 大陆像木筏一样在软层上慢慢漂开 → continental drift 大陆漂移

root: continental 源自拉丁语 continere（连在一起）；drift 源自古英语 drifan（驱动、被推动），本义指被水流或风力带走。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of continental drift. The thread runs from the hypothesis, to its evidence, to its missing mechanism, and finally to its place in plate tectonics.
sensesIntro.cn: continental drift 的八个义项。主线从假说，到证据，到缺失的机制，最后到它在板块构造中的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: continents separating slowly like rafts on a current.
core.cn: 核心意象：大陆像水流上的筏子一样缓慢分开。

branches.en: IDEA AND MOTION: the phrase names both the hypothesis and the process.
branches.cn: 想法与运动：这个短语既指假说，也指过程。

branches.en: ONE PROPOSAL: it is historically tied to Wegener's specific claim.
branches.cn: 一个提案：它在历史上与魏格纳的具体主张绑定。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: fitting coasts and shared fossils point to a former join.
branches.cn: 证据：海岸吻合与共享化石指向曾经的连接。

branches.en: THE GAP: a description of motion without a driver is incomplete.
branches.cn: 缺口：只描述运动而不给出驱动力的说法是不完整的。

branches.en: AFTERLIFE: absorbed by plate tectonics, and borrowed as a metaphor for slow separation.
branches.cn: 后续：被板块构造吸收，也被借作缓慢分离的比喻。

intro.en: The phrase is a noun compound of two independent words, so its 'affixes' are the pieces of each word and the related family they build.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个独立词构成名词复合体，因此它的构词分析就是两个词的构件及各自词族。

latinIntro.en: Continental is Latin-derived (continere), while drift is native English (Old English drifan). The two halves come from different language layers, and there is no single Latin family for drift, so latinEntries lists only the Latin side.
latinIntro.cn: continental 源自拉丁语（continere），drift 则是英语本族词（古英语 drifan）。两半来自不同语言层，drift 没有对应的拉丁词族，因此 latinEntries 只列拉丁语一侧。

items.example: Continental blocks moved apart over time.
items.exampleCN: 大陆块随时间分开。

items.structure: Old English drifan 'to drive', noun use of the verb
items.example: The raft drifted with the current.
items.exampleCN: 木筏随水流漂走。

items.meaning: to be carried along by a current or force
items.example: The continents drift a few centimetres a year.
items.exampleCN: 大陆每年漂移几厘米。

items.meaning: a person or thing that drifts
items.meaningCN: 漂流的人或物（-er 表示动作执行者）
items.example: The drifter had no fixed route.
items.exampleCN: 这个漂泊者没有固定路线。

items.example: Driftwood collected along the tide line.
items.exampleCN: 浮木沿着潮线堆积。

items.example: The slow drifting of continents is measured by satellites.
items.exampleCN: 大陆的缓慢漂移由卫星测量。

items.example: Continental fragments can be recognised by their fossils.
items.exampleCN: 大陆碎块可以通过化石识别。

items.example: The two landmasses drifted apart.
items.exampleCN: 两块陆地漂移分开。

definition_en: the act of two objects or groups hitting each other, or a serious disagreement
core_image: 两股物体迎面撞上，接触点爆出一圈冲击，双方都被迫改变方向
scene: 两块大陆板块迎面相撞，地面被挤得向上隆起。The collision of two plates pushed up a mountain range.
sceneCN: 这里 collision 指「碰撞」（第 2 个义项：两个板块相向撞击的地质过程）；句意为两个板块的碰撞抬升出一条山脉。

pos.zh: 碰撞；相撞；冲突；对撞

senses.title: Two objects hitting each other
senses.titleCN: 碰撞：两个物体撞在一起
senses.definition: the act of two moving objects hitting each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个运动物体相互撞击的动作
senses.example: The collision left a deep dent in both cars.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞在两辆车上都留下了深深的凹痕。
senses.why: The Latin verb collidere means 'to strike together', so the noun names the moment two paths meet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 collidere 意为「撞到一起」，所以这个名词命名两条路径相遇的瞬间。

senses.title: A plate collision
senses.titleCN: 板块碰撞：地质上的相向撞击
senses.definition: the meeting of two converging lithospheric plates
senses.definitionCN: 两个汇聚的岩石圈板块相遇
senses.example: The collision of two plates pushed up a mountain range.
senses.exampleCN: 两个板块的碰撞抬升出一条山脉。
senses.why: Plates travel toward each other at centimetres per year, and the contact compresses the crust between them.
senses.whyCN: 板块每年以厘米级速度相向而行，接触处把两者之间的地壳挤压起来。

senses.title: A celestial impact
senses.definition: the impact of one body in space with another
senses.definitionCN: 太空中一个天体与另一个天体的撞击
senses.example: A collision with an asteroid may have ended the age of the dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 一次小行星撞击可能终结了恐龙时代。
senses.why: Space objects follow paths that sometimes cross, and the meeting releases enormous energy.
senses.whyCN: 天体沿各自的路径运动，路径有时相交，相遇时便释放巨大能量。

senses.title: A particle collision
senses.definition: a high-energy meeting of subatomic particles
senses.definitionCN: 亚原子粒子之间的高能相遇
senses.example: The experiment records the debris of each particle collision.
senses.exampleCN: 实验记录每一次粒子对撞产生的碎片。
senses.why: Physicists collide particles deliberately so that the energy of contact reveals internal structure.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家有意让粒子对撞，以便用接触时的能量揭示内部结构。

senses.title: A traffic crash
senses.definition: a crash between vehicles or between a vehicle and an object
senses.definitionCN: 车辆之间或车辆与物体之间的撞击
senses.example: The report described a collision at the junction.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了路口的一起相撞事故。
senses.why: Vehicles are moving objects on fixed paths, so a crash is the everyday version of the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 车辆是沿固定路径运动的物体，所以车祸是这一通用义项的日常版本。

senses.title: A clash of interests
senses.definition: a serious disagreement between opposing interests or aims
senses.definitionCN: 对立利益或目标之间的严重不一致
senses.example: The plan created a collision between conservation and development.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划在保护与发展之间造成了冲突。
senses.why: Two aims that cannot both be satisfied meet head-on, just as two bodies do.
senses.whyCN: 两个无法同时满足的目标正面相遇，正如两个物体相撞。

senses.title: A clash of cultures
senses.definition: a sharp conflict between different cultures or beliefs
senses.definitionCN: 不同文化或信念之间的尖锐冲突
senses.example: The novel dramatises a collision of values.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把价值观的冲突戏剧化。
senses.why: The metaphor treats beliefs as bodies with incompatible directions.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把信念当作方向不相容的物体。

senses.title: Collision in computing
senses.definition: the case where two items map to the same location or path
senses.definitionCN: 两个项目映射到同一位置或路径的情形
senses.example: The program resolves a hash collision by chaining the entries.
senses.exampleCN: 程序用链式结构解决哈希碰撞。
senses.why: Two keys may land on one slot, so the technical sense keeps the same 'two things meeting at one point' shape.
senses.whyCN: 两个键可能落到同一个槽位，因此这个技术义保持「两物相遇于一点」的形状。

intro.en: Collision comes from Latin collidere 'to strike together', built from com- 'together' and laedere 'to strike'. The word moved from physical impact to conflict and then to technical uses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collision 来自拉丁语 collidere「撞到一起」，由 com-「共同」与 laedere「撞击」构成。这个词从物理撞击扩展到冲突，再扩展到技术用法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Laedere meant 'to strike, hurt, injure'; with com- 'together' it produced collidere 'to strike together, clash'.
items.cn: laedere 意为「撞击、伤害」；加上 com-「共同」就构成 collidere「撞到一起、冲突」。

items.en: Collisio, collisionis named the act of striking together, and its accusative collisionem passed into French and English.
items.cn: collisio, collisionis 指撞在一起的动作，其宾格 collisionem 传入法语与英语。

items.en: Old French collision and Middle English collision kept the physical sense and soon extended it to clashes of opinion.
items.cn: 古法语 collision 与中古英语 collision 保留了物理义，并很快扩展到意见冲突。

items.en: The word widened to cover conflicts of interest and personality as well as bodies.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到覆盖利益与性格冲突，而不仅是物体相撞。

items.en: Geology, astronomy and particle physics each adopted collision for their own kinds of impact, and computing added hash collisions.
items.cn: 地质学、天文学与粒子物理学各自采用 collision 指本领域的撞击，计算机领域又增加了哈希碰撞。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to collision; group two holds words for impact and disagreement that differ in force or scale.
note.cn: 第一组是形音接近 collision 的词；第二组是表示撞击或分歧但力度、尺度不同的词。

entries.definition: secret cooperation for a dishonest purpose; it comes from a different Latin verb meaning 'to play together'.
entries.definitionCN: 为不正当目的秘密合作；它来自另一个意为「一起玩」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: the force that holds something together; it is the opposite of hitting apart.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物聚在一起的力量；它与撞散相反。

entries.definition: the act of comparing or assembling texts; it belongs to a verb meaning 'to bring together'.
entries.definitionCN: 比对或汇编文本的动作；它属于另一个意为「带到一起」的动词。

entries.definition: the verb meaning 'to hit each other'; collision is its noun.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「相互撞击」的动词；collision 是它的名词。

entries.definition: a forceful hit, often one body striking another that is not moving toward it.
entries.definitionCN: 有力的撞击，常指一个物体撞上并未迎向它的物体。

entries.definition: a noisy collision, especially of vehicles; it emphasises sound and damage.
entries.definitionCN: 嘈杂的碰撞，尤指车辆；它强调声音与损坏。

entries.definition: a sharp disagreement or a noisy metallic collision; it often leans toward conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 尖锐的分歧或金属相撞的响声；常偏向冲突义。

entries.definition: a lasting struggle between opposing sides; collision is the moment of meeting, conflict is the state that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 对立双方持续的争斗；collision 是相遇的瞬间，conflict 是随后的状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin verbs and real usage contrasts, so the word is tied to its own family and to its neighbours.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词与真实的用法对照，因此这个词既连着自身词族，也连着近义词。

normal.en: collidere means strike together, so collision is the moment two paths meet.
normal.cn: collidere 表示撞到一起，所以 collision 就是两条路径相遇的瞬间。

normal.en: collision and collusion are near look-alikes with opposite meanings: one is hitting, the other is secretly plotting.
normal.cn: collision 与 collusion 形近而义反：一个是撞击，一个是秘密勾结。

normal.en: A plate collision raises mountains, which is why the Himalaya sits at a collision zone.
normal.cn: 板块碰撞抬起山脉，所以喜马拉雅山位于碰撞带。

normal.en: A collision is the meeting; a conflict is the state that may follow it.
normal.cn: collision 是相遇的瞬间，conflict 是可能随之而来的状态。

normal.en: A hash collision in computing is two keys landing in one slot, the same 'two at one point' shape.
normal.cn: 计算机里的哈希碰撞是两个键落到同一个槽位，仍是「两物在一点」的形状。

abstract.en: Abstractly, collision is a meeting that cannot be avoided: two trajectories share a point in space and time.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，collision 是无法回避的相遇：两条轨迹在空间与时间上共享一点。

abstract.en: From cars to plates to ideas, the constant is incompatibility plus contact.
abstract.cn: 从汽车到板块再到观念，不变的是「不相容」加「接触」。

abstract.en: Symbol: two arrows meeting at a single point, with a burst of lines at the contact.
abstract.cn: 符号：两个箭头在一点相遇，接触处爆出一圈短线。

examples.en: The collision between the two plates formed the Himalaya.
examples.cn: 两个板块之间的碰撞形成了喜马拉雅山。

examples.en: The car was damaged in a collision with a truck.
examples.cn: 这辆车在与卡车相撞时受损。

examples.en: The debate revealed a collision of values.
examples.cn: 这场辩论暴露出价值观的冲突。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扣里钻」—— 两辆车扣在一起往里钻，撞成一团 → collision 碰撞

root: 源自拉丁语 collidere（撞到一起），由 com-（共同）与 laedere（撞击）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of collision. All keep the shape of two courses meeting at one point, from plates to particles to ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: collision 的八个义项都保持「两条路径在一点相遇」的形状，从板块到粒子再到观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths meeting at one point with a burst of force.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路径在一点相遇，并迸发出力。

branches.en: TRAFFIC IMPACT: vehicles meeting at speed show the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 交通撞击：车辆高速相遇，是最日常的碰撞。

branches.en: PLANETARY IMPACT: plates and asteroids collide at their own scale.
branches.cn: 行星尺度撞击：板块与小行星在各自尺度上相撞。

branches.en: HUMAN CONFLICT: interests and values meet head-on like bodies.
branches.cn: 人类冲突：利益与价值观像物体一样正面相遇。

branches.en: TECHNICAL CLASH: two items map to one location.
branches.cn: 技术冲突：两个项目映射到同一位置。

branches.en: THE COMMON FORM: two bodies and two particles meet at one point.
branches.cn: 共同形态：两个物体与两个粒子都在一点相遇。

intro.en: Collision has a compact Latin family: the verb collide, the adjective collisional, the instrument collider and the negative compound anticollision.
intro.cn: collision 有一个紧凑的拉丁词族：动词 collide、形容词 collisional、工具名 collider 以及否定复合词 anticollision。

latinIntro.en: Latin laedere 'to strike' with com- 'together' gives collidere and its noun collisio; the same root appears in lesion and in the negative sense of 'hurt'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laedere「撞击」加 com-「共同」产生 collidere 及其名词 collisio；同一词根也出现在 lesion 中，并保留「伤害」的否定含义。

items.example: The prefix makes the striking mutual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使撞击成为相互的。

items.example: The root also survives in lesion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也保留在 lesion 中。

items.meaning: to hit each other; to clash
items.example: The two plates collide along the trench.
items.exampleCN: 两个板块沿海沟相撞。

items.meaning: relating to or caused by collision
items.meaningCN: 与碰撞有关的，或由碰撞引起的
items.example: Collisional heating melted the crust.
items.exampleCN: 碰撞加热使地壳熔融。

items.meaning: a machine that makes particles collide
items.meaningCN: 使粒子对撞的机器（-er 表示工具）
items.example: The collider accelerates protons to high energy.
items.exampleCN: 这台对撞机把质子加速到高能。

items.example: The car has an anticollision system.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车装有防撞系统。

items.meaning: the belt where two plates collide
items.example: The collision zone is seismically active.
items.exampleCN: 这个碰撞带地震活动活跃。

items.meaning: a path that will lead to a collision
items.example: The two ships were on a collision course.
items.exampleCN: 两艘船处在相撞的航线上。

items.example: The hull showed collision damage.
items.exampleCN: 船体上有碰撞造成的损坏。

definition_en: to hit something or someone while moving, or to be in serious disagreement
core_image: 两个运动中的物体沿不同路线行进，在一点上撞上，速度与方向都被打乱
scene: 两个板块每年只移动几厘米，却在漫长的年代里撞到了一起。Two plates collide slowly, and the edge of one sinks beneath the other.
sceneCN: 这里 collide 指「相撞」（第 1 个义项：两个运动物体撞在一起）；句意为两个板块缓慢相撞，其中一个的边缘沉到另一个之下。

pos.zh: 相撞；碰撞；冲突
使相撞（较少用）

senses.title: Two objects hit each other
senses.titleCN: 相撞：两个运动物体撞在一起
senses.definition: to hit another moving object while travelling
senses.definitionCN: 在行进中撞上另一个运动物体
senses.example: Two plates collide slowly, and the edge of one sinks beneath the other.
senses.exampleCN: 两个板块缓慢相撞，其中一个的边缘沉到另一个之下。
senses.why: Collidere is com- 'together' plus laedere 'to strike', so the verb describes two paths ending in one contact.
senses.whyCN: collidere 是 com-「共同」加 laedere「撞击」，所以这个动词描述两条路径终结于一次接触。

senses.title: Plates collide
senses.definition: of lithospheric plates, to move toward each other and meet
senses.definitionCN: 岩石圈板块相向运动并相遇
senses.example: The two continents collided and closed the ocean between them.
senses.exampleCN: 两块大陆相撞，把它们之间的海洋闭合了。
senses.why: Plate motion is slow but continuous, so collision is the inevitable result where two vectors point at each other.
senses.whyCN: 板块运动缓慢而持续，因此当两个速度向量相对时，碰撞就是必然结果。

senses.title: Particles collide
senses.definition: of subatomic particles, to meet at high energy
senses.definitionCN: 亚原子粒子以高能相遇
senses.example: Physicists collide protons to study the forces inside them.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家让质子对撞，以研究其内部的力。
senses.why: The experiment forces two beams onto one path, which is the literal sense of striking together.
senses.whyCN: 实验把两束粒子引到同一条路径上，这正是「撞到一起」的字面义。

senses.title: Vehicles collide
senses.definition: of vehicles, to crash into each other
senses.definitionCN: 车辆相互撞击
senses.example: The two cars collided at the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 两辆车在路口相撞。
senses.why: Vehicles follow separate tracks until one track cuts across another, which is the everyday form of the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 车辆各行其道，直到一条路线横切另一条，这就是通用义项的日常形态。

senses.title: Opinions or interests clash
senses.definition: of ideas, interests or aims, to be in direct opposition
senses.definitionCN: 想法、利益或目标直接对立
senses.example: Their views on the project collided at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这个项目的看法在会上发生了冲突。
senses.why: Two positions that cannot both hold are like two bodies on the same path: they cannot pass through each other.
senses.whyCN: 两个不能同时成立的立场就像同一条路上的两个物体：无法互相穿过。

senses.title: Schedules collide
senses.definition: of times or events, to fall at the same moment so that both cannot be attended
senses.definitionCN: 时间或事件落在同一时刻，无法同时参加
senses.example: My lecture collides with the lab session.
senses.exampleCN: 我的讲座与实验课时间冲突。
senses.why: Two appointments on one clock are two objects on one point, so the verb extends naturally to time.
senses.whyCN: 同一时钟上的两个安排就是同一点上的两个物体，所以这个动词自然延伸到时间。

senses.title: Celestial bodies collide
senses.definition: of bodies in space, to impact one another
senses.definitionCN: 太空中的天体相互撞击
senses.example: A comet may collide with a planet over millions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 彗星可能在数百万年间与行星相撞。
senses.why: Orbits are paths, and where two orbits cross there is a chance of contact.
senses.whyCN: 轨道就是路径，两条轨道相交处就有接触的可能。

senses.title: An elastic collision
senses.definition: in physics, to exchange momentum in a collision that conserves kinetic energy
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中，于保持动能的碰撞里交换动量
senses.example: Two billiard balls collide and rebound without losing energy.
senses.exampleCN: 两个台球相撞后弹开，能量没有损失。
senses.why: The technical sense narrows the contact to a measurable exchange of momentum and energy.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义把接触收窄为可测量的动量与能量交换。

intro.en: Collide is the verb behind collision. Both come from Latin collidere 'to strike together', a compound of 'together' and 'to strike'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collide 是 collision 背后的动词。两者都来自拉丁语 collidere「撞到一起」，由「共同」与「撞击」复合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Com- meant 'together' and laedere meant 'to strike, hurt'; the compound collidere meant 'to strike together, clash'.
items.cn: com- 意为「共同」，laedere 意为「撞击、伤害」；复合词 collidere 意为「撞到一起、冲突」。

items.en: The verb had collisi as its past stem and collisum as its participle, which is why the English noun is collision rather than collidement.
items.cn: 这个动词的过去词干是 collisi，分词是 collisum，这就是英语名词采用 collision 而不是 collidement 的原因。

items.en: French inherited the verb as collider and the noun as collision, both formed on the Latin supine stem.
items.cn: 法语继承了这个动词 collider 与名词 collision，两者都建立在拉丁语动名词词干上。

items.en: English borrowed the noun first and later formed or borrowed the verb collide; early uses described physical impact.
items.cn: 英语先借入名词，后来才形成或借入动词 collide；早期用法描述物理撞击。

items.en: The verb widened to conflicts of opinion, of schedules and of interests, and physics added the precise sense of momentum exchange.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到意见、日程与利益的冲突，物理学又增加了动量交换的精确义。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that look or sound close to collide; group two holds verbs of hitting and disagreeing that differ in force or focus.
note.cn: 第一组是形音接近 collide 的动词；第二组是表示撞击或分歧但力度与侧重不同的动词。

entries.definition: to plot secretly with someone; it comes from a different Latin verb meaning 'to play together'.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人秘密勾结；它来自另一个意为「一起玩」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: to happen at the same time or occupy the same space; it stresses agreement, not impact.
entries.definitionCN: 同时发生或占据同一空间；它强调一致，而非撞击。

entries.definition: to bring something to an end or to decide after reasoning; it has nothing to do with impact.
entries.definitionCN: 结束某事，或经推理后决定；与撞击无关。

entries.definition: the noun of collide; the verb describes the act and the noun names the event.
entries.definitionCN: collide 的名词；动词描述动作，名词命名事件。

entries.definition: to hit something violently and noisily, especially in a vehicle; it stresses damage and sound.
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈而有声地撞上某物，尤指车辆；它强调损坏与声音。

entries.definition: to come into conflict, or to strike with a loud metallic sound; the disagreement sense is stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 发生冲突，或发出金属撞击声；它的分歧义更强。

entries.definition: to strike something with force; one body acts and the other receives.
entries.definitionCN: 用力击打某物；一方施力，另一方承受。

entries.definition: to touch or knock lightly; collide implies more speed and force.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻碰触或撞到；collide 含有更大的速度与力量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real physics, so the verb can be connected to its noun and to its technical sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件与真实的物理，因此这个动词可以连到它的名词与技术义。

normal.en: collide is com- plus laedere: strike together. The noun is collision, not collidement, because English took the Latin stem.
normal.cn: collide 是 com- 加 laedere：撞到一起。名词是 collision 而不是 collidement，因为英语采用了拉丁词干。

normal.en: collide and collude look alike but one is hitting and the other is plotting.
normal.cn: collide 与 collude 形近，但一个是撞击，一个是密谋。

normal.en: Plates collide, particles collide, cars collide, schedules collide: in every case two paths share one point.
normal.cn: 板块相撞、粒子对撞、汽车相撞、日程冲突：每种情形都是两条路径共享一点。

normal.en: An elastic collision keeps kinetic energy; an inelastic one turns some of it into heat.
normal.cn: 弹性碰撞保持动能；非弹性碰撞把一部分动能变成热。

normal.en: In physics the verb is often used where the noun collision would also fit, so the pair can be learned together.
normal.cn: 在物理学中，用动词的地方通常也能用名词 collision，因此这一对可以一起记。

abstract.en: Abstractly, collide means two courses cannot stay separate: their paths cross at one point.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，collide 表示两条路线无法再分开：它们的路径在一点交叉。

abstract.en: The verb always implies motion before contact, which is why it suits both rocks and opinions.
abstract.cn: 这个动词总隐含接触之前的运动，所以它既适合岩石，也适合观点。

abstract.en: Symbol: two arrows entering one point from different directions, with a short rebound arrow after contact.
abstract.cn: 符号：两个箭头从不同方向进入同一点，接触后出现一条短的回弹箭头。

examples.en: The two plates collided and formed a high plateau.
examples.cn: 两个板块相撞，形成了一片高高原。

examples.en: The trucks collided on the icy bridge.
examples.cn: 卡车在结冰的桥上相撞。

examples.en: Her talk collides with my afternoon class.
examples.cn: 她的报告与我的下午课程冲突。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扣来」—— 两辆车扣在一起拉过来，撞上 → collide 相撞

root: 源自拉丁语 collidere（撞到一起），由 com-（共同）与 laedere（撞击）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of collide. The thread is motion ending in contact, whether the bodies are plates, particles, cars or opinions.
sensesIntro.cn: collide 的八个义项。主线是运动终结于接触，无论对象是板块、粒子、汽车还是观点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two moving paths meeting at one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条运动路径在一点相遇。

branches.en: VEHICLE CONTACT: cars hit at everyday speeds.
branches.cn: 车辆接触：汽车以日常速度互撞。

branches.en: LARGE-SCALE CONTACT: plates and celestial bodies collide over immense spans.
branches.cn: 大尺度接触：板块与天体在漫长时间与空间中相撞。

branches.en: PARTICLE CONTACT: particles meet at high energy.
branches.cn: 粒子接触：粒子以高能相遇。

branches.en: NON-PHYSICAL CONTACT: opinions and schedules occupy one point and cannot both proceed.
branches.cn: 非物理接触：观点与日程占据同一点，无法同时推进。

branches.en: OUTCOME: contact redirects motion and shares momentum, whether the bodies bounce apart or deform.
branches.cn: 结果：无论弹开还是变形，接触都会改变运动方向并分享动量。

intro.en: Collide builds a small Latin family around one root for striking, with a verb, a noun, an instrument and an adjective.
intro.cn: collide 围绕一个「撞击」词根构成一个小型拉丁词族，包括动词、名词、工具名与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin laedere 'to strike' plus com- 'together' gives collidere; its supine stem collis- supplies collision, collisional and collider.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laedere「撞击」加 com-「共同」构成 collidere；其动名词词干 collis- 提供 collision、collisional 与 collider。

items.example: The prefix makes the striking mutual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使撞击成为相互的。

items.example: The root survives in lesion as well.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也保留在 lesion 中。

items.meaningCN: 撞在一起的事件（-ion 构成事件名词）
items.example: The collision cracked the windscreen.
items.exampleCN: 碰撞震裂了挡风玻璃。

items.meaning: caused by or relating to collision
items.meaningCN: 由碰撞引起的，或与碰撞有关的
items.example: Collisional belts thicken the crust.
items.exampleCN: 碰撞带使地壳增厚。

items.example: The collider ran through the night.
items.exampleCN: 这台对撞机整夜运行。

items.meaning: in the act of hitting each other
items.example: Colliding plates raise mountain belts.
items.exampleCN: 相撞的板块抬起山脉带。

items.example: The asteroid collided with the planet.
items.exampleCN: 小行星撞上了这颗行星。

items.example: Anticollision radar warned the pilot.
items.exampleCN: 防撞雷达向飞行员发出警告。

definition_zh: 俯冲；一个板块向下插入另一个板块之下的过程
definition_en: the process by which one lithospheric plate sinks beneath another
core_image: 一块坚硬的板片斜插进另一块板片下方，像把一张硬卡纸沿桌面边缘折下去
scene: 海沟处，古老的洋底不断被带入地下。Along the trench, subduction carries old ocean floor down into the mantle.
sceneCN: 这里 subduction 指「俯冲」（第 1 个义项：一个板块向下插入另一个板块之下的过程）；句意为沿海沟一带，俯冲把古老洋底带入地幔。

pos.zh: 俯冲（作用）；俯冲带；消减

collocations.zh: 与俯冲有关的火山作用

senses.title: One plate sinking beneath another
senses.titleCN: 俯冲：一个板块沉入另一个板块之下
senses.definition: the process by which one lithospheric plate descends beneath another
senses.definitionCN: 一个岩石圈板块向下插入另一个板块之下的过程
senses.example: Along the trench, subduction carries old ocean floor down into the mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海沟一带，俯冲把古老洋底带入地幔。
senses.why: Latin subducere means 'to lead under', so subduction is the act of one plate being led beneath another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 subducere 意为「向下引导」，所以俯冲就是一个板块被引到另一个板块之下的动作。

senses.title: The subduction zone
senses.titleCN: 俯冲带：俯冲发生的狭长地带
senses.definition: the long belt where one plate descends beneath another
senses.definitionCN: 一个板块向另一个板块之下下沉的狭长带
senses.example: The subduction zone lies offshore, marked by a deep trench.
senses.exampleCN: 俯冲带位于近海，由一条深海沟标出。
senses.why: Because the process is localised at a boundary, the noun can name the place as well as the action.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个过程局限在边界上，这个名词既可指动作，也可指地点。

senses.title: Consumption of crust
senses.titleCN: 地壳消减：物质回到地幔
senses.definition: the return of crustal material to the mantle, which balances crust created at ridges
senses.definitionCN: 地壳物质回到地幔，与洋中脊新生的地壳相平衡
senses.example: Subduction removes ocean floor as fast as ridges create it.
senses.exampleCN: 俯冲消减洋底的速度与洋中脊生成的速度相当。
senses.why: A planet cannot grow new crust forever, so the descending plate must be recycled.
senses.whyCN: 行星不能永远生成新地壳，因此下行的板块必须被回收。

senses.title: The cause of arc volcanoes
senses.definition: the process that adds water to the mantle wedge and triggers melting
senses.definitionCN: 把水带入地幔楔并触发熔融的过程
senses.example: Subduction feeds the volcanoes of the Pacific arcs.
senses.exampleCN: 俯冲为太平洋岛弧的火山提供物质。
senses.why: Water released from the sinking slab lowers the melting point of the mantle above, so magma rises behind the trench.
senses.whyCN: 下沉板片释放的水降低了上方地幔的熔点，于是岩浆在海沟后方上升。

senses.title: The cause of great earthquakes
senses.definition: the locking and sudden slipping of the contact between two plates
senses.definitionCN: 两个板块接触面锁住后又突然滑动的过程
senses.example: The subduction interface can rupture over hundreds of kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 俯冲界面可以断裂数百公里。
senses.why: The contact is a fault that stays stuck for centuries and then breaks in seconds.
senses.whyCN: 这个接触面是一条会卡住数百年的断层，然后在几秒内破裂。

senses.title: The angle and style of descent
senses.definition: the dip of the descending slab, which varies from shallow to steep
senses.definitionCN: 下行板片的倾角，可从平缓到陡立
senses.example: Steep subduction produces a narrow volcanic arc.
senses.exampleCN: 陡倾的俯冲产生狭窄的火山弧。
senses.why: The slab does not sink straight down; its angle controls where melt and earthquakes appear.
senses.whyCN: 板片并不垂直下沉；它的角度决定熔融与地震出现的位置。

senses.title: An ancient subduction record
senses.definition: the preserved remains of a former subduction zone in the rock record
senses.definitionCN: 岩石记录中保存下来的旧俯冲带遗迹
senses.example: Blueschist belts mark ancient subduction.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝片岩带标记着古俯冲作用。
senses.why: High-pressure, low-temperature rocks form only where cold crust is pushed deep, so their presence records a past trench.
senses.whyCN: 高压低温岩石只在冷地壳被推入深处时形成，因此它们的存在记录了过去的深海沟。

senses.title: A planetary recycling engine
senses.definition: the mechanism that exchanges material between surface and interior on a rocky planet
senses.definitionCN: 在岩石行星上交换地表与内部物质的机制
senses.example: Subduction is why Earth's interior and surface keep exchanging material.
senses.exampleCN: 俯冲正是地球内部与地表持续交换物质的原因。
senses.why: Without a descending limb, the planet would store water and carbon at the surface instead of cycling them.
senses.whyCN: 没有下行的一环，行星就会把水与碳留在地表，而不是让它们循环。

intro.en: Subduction is a Latin-derived noun built on subducere 'to lead under'. Geology adopted it for the descent of one plate beneath another. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subduction 是由拉丁语 subducere「向下引导」构成的派生名词。地质学用它指一个板块向另一个板块之下下沉。年代均为约数。

items.en: Subducere combines sub- 'under, from below' with ducere 'to lead, draw'; it meant 'to draw away, take away, lead under'.
items.cn: subducere 由 sub-「在下、从下面」与 ducere「引导、拉」构成，意为「拉走、带走、向下引」。

items.en: Subductio, subductionis meant 'a drawing away or removal'; the geological sense is much later and much narrower.
items.cn: subductio, subductionis 意为「拉走、移除」；地质义要晚得多，也窄得多。

items.en: English first used subduction in general senses of removal or withdrawal, without any geological meaning.
items.cn: 英语最初把 subduction 用于一般的「移除、撤回」义，不含地质含义。

items.en: With plate tectonics, the word was fixed to the descent of oceanic lithosphere beneath another plate.
items.cn: 随着板块构造学说，这个词被固定指大洋岩石圈向另一板块之下下沉。

items.en: Subduction now usually implies a trench, a descending slab, arc volcanism and a seismic zone, all at one boundary.
items.cn: 现代用法中，subduction 通常同时暗示海沟、下行板片、岛弧火山作用与地震带，且都在同一边界上。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the -duction shape but come from different verbs; group two holds the boundary processes that are often mixed with subduction.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 -duction 外形但来自不同动词的词；第二组是常与俯冲混淆的边界过程。

entries.definition: the arithmetic operation of taking one number from another; it comes from trahere 'to draw', not ducere.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个数中减去另一个数的算术运算；它来自 trahere「拉」，不是 ducere。

entries.definition: the act of carrying someone away; ab- 'away' plus ducere gives a different direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把人带走的行为；ab-「离开」加 ducere 给出另一个方向。

entries.definition: the act of making something; pro- 'forward' plus ducere means leading forward.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的行为；pro-「向前」加 ducere 意为向前引出。

entries.definition: the act of making smaller; re- 'back' plus ducere means leading back.
entries.definitionCN: 使变小；re-「向后」加 ducere 意为引回。

entries.definition: the approach of two plates toward each other; subduction is one result of convergence.
entries.definitionCN: 两个板块相互靠近；俯冲是汇聚的一种结果。

entries.definition: the act of going down; it describes the direction without naming plates.
entries.definitionCN: 向下运动；它描述方向，不指板块。

entries.definition: the sliding of one plate beneath another along a thrust fault; it stresses the fault motion.
entries.definitionCN: 一个板块沿逆冲断层滑到另一个之下；它强调断层运动。

entries.definition: the pushing of oceanic crust onto a continent instead of beneath it.
entries.definitionCN: 把洋壳推到大陆之上，而不是推到大陆之下。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin direction prefixes and real boundary processes, so the word is not confused with its look-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁方向前缀与真实的边界过程，因此这个词不会与形近词混淆。

normal.en: sub- means under and ducere means lead, so subduction is leading a plate under another.
normal.cn: sub- 表示在下，ducere 表示引导，所以俯冲就是把一个板块引到另一个之下。

normal.en: The -duction words split by verb: subduction and abduction from ducere, subtraction from trahere.
normal.cn: 带 -duction 的词按动词分家：subduction 与 abduction 来自 ducere，subtraction 来自 trahere。

normal.en: A subduction zone has three signatures: a deep trench, arc volcanoes and a dipping seismic zone.
normal.cn: 俯冲带的三项标志是：深海沟、岛弧火山与倾斜的地震带。

normal.en: Subduction balances spreading: what ridges create, trenches consume.
normal.cn: 俯冲与扩张相平衡：洋中脊生成多少，海沟就消减多少。

normal.en: Water from the slab lowers the melting point above it, which is why arc volcanoes stand behind the trench.
normal.cn: 板片带来的水降低了上方地幔的熔点，所以岛弧火山立在海沟后方。

abstract.en: Abstractly, subduction is a downward exit: material leaves the surface system and returns to the interior.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，subduction 是一条向下的出口：物质离开地表系统，回到内部。

abstract.en: The word pairs direction with recycling, so it names both a route and a planetary budget.
abstract.cn: 这个词把方向与循环配在一起，因此它既命名一条路线，也命名一笔行星尺度的收支。

abstract.en: Symbol: an arrow bending down under a horizontal bar and disappearing into a shaded layer.
abstract.cn: 符号：一条箭头在水平横条下折向下，并消失在阴影层中。

examples.en: Subduction zones produce the deepest earthquakes on Earth.
examples.cn: 俯冲带产生地球上最深的地震。

examples.en: The subduction of oceanic lithosphere closes ocean basins over time.
examples.cn: 大洋岩石圈的俯冲随时间关闭大洋盆地。

examples.en: Geologists mapped an ancient subduction zone in the mountain belt.
examples.cn: 地质学家在山脉带中测绘出一条古俯冲带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub 在下 + duct 引导」—— 把板片引到下面去 → subduction 俯冲

root: 源自拉丁语 subducere（向下引导、拉走），由 sub-（在下）与 ducere（引导）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of subduction. The thread is a downward route: a plate goes under, crust is consumed, and water and rock return to the interior.
sensesIntro.cn: subduction 的八个义项。主线是一条向下的路线：板块下插、地壳被消减、水与岩石回到内部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slab bending down and disappearing under another slab.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块板片向下弯折，消失在另一块板片之下。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PLACE: the same word names the sinking and the belt where it happens.
branches.cn: 过程与地点：同一个词既指下沉，也指发生下沉的带。

branches.en: RECYCLING: consumption at trenches balances creation at ridges.
branches.cn: 循环：海沟处的消减与洋中脊的生成相平衡。

branches.en: WATER AND MELT: the slab releases water, and the mantle above melts.
branches.cn: 水与熔融：板片释放水，上方的地幔因此熔融。

branches.en: GEOMETRY OF RUPTURE: the dip of the contact controls where quakes occur.
branches.cn: 破裂的几何：接触面的倾角控制地震发生的位置。

branches.en: FOSSIL TRENCHES: high-pressure belts record where old slabs once sank.
branches.cn: 化石海沟：高压岩带记录旧板片曾经下沉的位置。

intro.en: Subduction is built from a Latin direction prefix, a verb root for leading, and a noun suffix, and the same pieces recur in many English words.
intro.cn: subduction 由拉丁方向前缀、表示「引导」的动词词根与名词后缀构成，这些成分在大量英语词中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Sub- 'under' plus ducere 'to lead' gives subducere, whose supine stem subduct- supplies subduction; the same ducere family includes conduct, produce and reduce.
latinIntro.cn: sub-「在下」加 ducere「引导」构成 subducere，其动名词词干 subduct- 提供 subduction；同一 ducere 词族还包括 conduct、produce 与 reduce。

items.example: The prefix sets the direction of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀设定动作的方向。

items.example: The root builds conduct and produce as well.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也构成 conduct 与 produce。

items.meaning: the act or result of a verb
items.meaningCN: 动词的动作或结果（名词后缀）
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The dense slab subducts beneath the continent.
items.exampleCN: 致密的板片俯冲到大陆之下。

items.meaning: in the process of sinking beneath
items.example: The subducting slab releases water.
items.exampleCN: 正在俯冲的板片释放水。

items.meaningCN: 已被带入另一板块之下的
items.example: Subducted crust is recycled into the mantle.
items.exampleCN: 已被俯冲的地壳被回收到地幔。

items.meaning: the belt where a plate descends
items.example: The subduction zone is marked by a trench.
items.exampleCN: 俯冲带以一条海沟为标志。

items.example: Subductional earthquakes can be very deep.
items.exampleCN: 俯冲地震可以非常深。

items.example: Paleosubduction is inferred from high-pressure rocks.
items.exampleCN: 古俯冲由高压岩石推断出来。

definition_zh: 使俯冲；（板块）俯冲；消减；使（眼球）下转
definition_en: to carry one lithospheric plate beneath another; also to turn an eye downward
core_image: 一只手把一张硬纸片从桌面边缘往下折进去，纸片没入桌面之下
scene: 两个板块相遇时，较致密的那一块会向下插进去。When two plates meet, the denser one may subduct beneath the other.
sceneCN: 这里 subduct 指「俯冲」（第 1 个义项：板块向下插入另一板块之下）；句意为两个板块相遇时，较致密的一块可能俯冲到另一块之下。

pos.zh: 使向下插入；使（眼球）下转
（板块）俯冲；消减

senses.title: To carry a plate beneath another
senses.titleCN: 俯冲：把一个板块带到另一板块之下
senses.definition: to carry one lithospheric plate down beneath another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个岩石圈板块向下带到另一个板块之下
senses.example: When two plates meet, the denser one may subduct beneath the other.
senses.exampleCN: 两个板块相遇时，较致密的一块可能俯冲到另一块之下。
senses.why: Subducere is 'lead under', so the verb profiles the downward route of the plate.
senses.whyCN: subducere 意为「向下引导」，所以这个动词突出板块的向下路线。

senses.title: Of a plate, to sink
senses.definition: of a plate, to descend by its own weight into the mantle
senses.definitionCN: 板块靠自身重量下沉进入地幔
senses.example: Old, cold ocean floor subducts readily because it is dense.
senses.exampleCN: 古老寒冷的洋底因密度大而容易俯冲。
senses.why: The verb is used intransitively when the plate is the actor: it subducts, it does not get subducted.
senses.whyCN: 当板块是动作主体时，这个动词作不及物用：它俯冲，而不是被俯冲。

senses.title: To consume crust
senses.definition: to remove crustal material from the surface by carrying it down
senses.definitionCN: 把地壳物质向下带走，从而使其离开地表
senses.example: The trench subducts more sediment than the ridge can replace.
senses.exampleCN: 海沟消减的沉积物超过洋中脊能补充的量。
senses.why: The downward route also removes material from the surface budget, which is why the process is called consumption.
senses.whyCN: 向下的路线也把物质从地表收支中移除，所以这个过程被称为消减。

senses.title: To turn an eye downward
senses.definition: in medicine, to turn the eye downward
senses.definitionCN: 在医学中，使眼球向下转动
senses.example: The examiner subducted the eye to inspect the lower lid.
senses.exampleCN: 检查者使眼球下转，以便查看下眼睑。
senses.why: This medical sense uses the same 'lead down' image for a small, controlled movement.
senses.whyCN: 这个医学义用同一个「向下引导」的形象，只是动作更小、更受控。

senses.title: To draw something downward
senses.definition: to draw or pull something downward
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向下拉或向下移
senses.example: The surgeon subducted the tissue to reach the deeper layer.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生把组织向下拉，以到达更深的层次。
senses.why: The general sense is the literal core: sub- plus ducere is simply 'lead under or down'.
senses.whyCN: 一般义就是字面核心：sub- 加 ducere 就是「向下或向里引导」。

senses.title: The subducting slab
senses.definition: the participial use describing a slab that is descending
senses.definitionCN: 用分词描述正在下沉的板片
senses.example: The subducting slab bends as it enters the mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 俯冲板片在进入地幔时发生弯曲。
senses.why: The participle keeps the verb's direction and adds ongoing aspect, so it names the moving plate itself.
senses.whyCN: 分词保留动词的方向并增添进行意味，因此它直接命名正在运动的板片。

senses.title: To carry water and sediment down
senses.titleCN: 把水与沉积物带入地下
senses.definition: to carry water, sediment or carbon into the mantle with the plate
senses.definitionCN: 随板块把水、沉积物或碳带入地幔
senses.example: Subducted sediment carries carbon deep into the Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 被俯冲的沉积物把碳带入地球深部。
senses.why: The plate is not pure rock; whatever lies on it travels with it, so the verb covers the whole cargo.
senses.whyCN: 板块不是纯岩石；它上面的一切都随之移动，所以这个动词覆盖整批「货物」。

senses.title: The passive result
senses.titleCN: 被动结果：已被带入地下
senses.definition: the past-participial sense of material that has already been carried down
senses.definitionCN: 过去分词义：已经被带入地下的物质
senses.example: Subducted basalts reappear in island-arc lavas.
senses.exampleCN: 被俯冲的玄武岩会以岛弧熔岩的形式重新出现。
senses.why: Once the descent is complete, the participle describes the material's new state rather than its motion.
senses.whyCN: 一旦下沉完成，分词描述的就是物质的新状态，而不是它的运动。

intro.en: Subduct is the verb behind subduction, from Latin subducere 'to lead under'. Its geological sense is modern, while its medical sense is older than plate tectonics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subduct 是 subduction 背后的动词，来自拉丁语 subducere「向下引导」。它的地质义是现代用法，而医学义比板块构造学说更早。年代均为约数。

items.en: Subducere combined sub- 'under' with ducere 'to lead'; it meant 'to draw away, withdraw, lead under'.
items.cn: subducere 把 sub-「在下」与 ducere「引导」组合起来，意为「拉走、撤回、向下引」。

items.en: The past participle subductus 'drawn away, led under' is the form English used for the adjective subducted.
items.cn: 过去分词 subductus「被拉走、被向下引」就是英语形容词 subducted 所用的形式。

items.en: English used subduct for drawing something away or down, including medical descriptions of eye movement.
items.cn: 英语用 subduct 指把某物拉走或拉下，包括医学中对眼球运动的描述。

items.en: Plate tectonics gave the verb its dominant modern sense: a plate descends beneath another.
items.cn: 板块构造学说赋予这个动词现代的主要义项：一个板块向另一个板块之下下沉。

items.en: The verb is now commoner as subducting or subducted than as a finite verb, because the moving plate is usually described as an ongoing process.
items.cn: 现在这个动词多以 subducting 或 subducted 形式出现，而少作限定动词，因为运动的板片通常被描述为持续过程。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that share the sub- prefix but take different roots; group two holds verbs of downward motion with a different focus.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 sub- 前缀但词根不同的动词；第二组是侧重不同的向下运动动词。

entries.definition: to take one number away from another; the root is trahere 'to draw', not ducere.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个数中减去另一个数；词根是 trahere「拉」，不是 ducere。

entries.definition: to carry someone away; ab- 'away' reverses the direction of sub-.
entries.definitionCN: 把人带走；ab-「离开」把 sub- 的方向反过来。

entries.definition: to take an amount away; de- 'down from' gives a subtractive sense.
entries.definitionCN: 扣除一笔数额；de-「从……下来」给出减去的意思。

entries.definition: to lead or guide; con- 'together' plus ducere means lead together.
entries.definitionCN: 引导、指挥；con-「共同」加 ducere 意为一起引导。

entries.definition: to go down; it gives the direction but not the plate setting.
entries.definitionCN: 向下走；它给出方向，但不含板块语境。

entries.definition: to go down through a fluid or soft material; subduct adds the image of sliding under a plate.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过流体或软物质向下；subduct 增添了滑到板块之下的形象。

entries.definition: to slide beneath another plate along a thrust fault; it stresses the fault rather than the slab.
entries.definitionCN: 沿逆冲断层滑到另一个板块之下；它强调断层而非板片。

entries.definition: to come together; plates converge before one subducts.
entries.definitionCN: 靠拢；板块先汇聚，然后其中一个俯冲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin direction and root contrasts, so subduct is separated from subtract, abduct and conduct.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁方向与词根对照，因此 subduct 能与 subtract、abduct、conduct 分开。

normal.en: sub- is under and ducere is lead: subduct is lead under, while abduct is lead away.
normal.cn: sub- 是在下，ducere 是引导：subduct 是向下引，abduct 是带走。

normal.en: subtract belongs to trahere, not ducere, which is why it means take away a number rather than lead under.
normal.cn: subtract 属于 trahere 而不是 ducere，所以它是减去一个数，而不是向下引。

normal.en: The participle subducted describes crust that has already gone down; the participle subducting describes the plate on its way down.
normal.cn: 分词 subducted 描述已经下去的地壳；分词 subducting 描述正在下行的板片。

normal.en: The medical sense subduct an eye is a small controlled version of the same downward lead.
normal.cn: 医学用法 subduct an eye 是同一个「向下引导」的小型受控版本。

normal.en: A subducting slab carries water and sediment with it, so the verb covers the whole cargo, not just the rock.
normal.cn: 俯冲板片带着水与沉积物一起下去，所以这个动词覆盖整批货物，而不只是岩石。

abstract.en: Abstractly, subduct means move something out of sight by putting it under something else.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，subduct 表示把某物放到另一样东西下面，使它从视野中消失。

abstract.en: The root contrast teaches direction: sub- goes under, ab- goes away, de- goes down from, con- goes together.
abstract.cn: 词根对照教人方向：sub- 向下，ab- 离开，de- 从……下来，con- 一起。

abstract.en: Symbol: a horizontal bar with an arrow sliding under its edge and turning downward.
abstract.cn: 符号：一条横杆，一支箭头从杆边滑入并转向下方。

examples.en: The dense oceanic plate subducts beneath the lighter continental plate.
examples.cn: 致密的洋板块俯冲到较轻的陆板块之下。

examples.en: Subducted sediments release water into the mantle wedge.
examples.cn: 被俯冲的沉积物把水释放到地幔楔中。

examples.en: The doctor subducted the eye to examine the lower lid.
examples.cn: 医生使眼球下转以检查下眼睑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub 下 + duct 管道」—— 像管道一样把板片引到下面 → subduct 俯冲

root: 源自拉丁语 subducere（向下引导、拉走），由 sub-（在下）与 ducere（引导）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of subduct. The thread is leading something under: a plate, a cargo of water and sediment, or an eye turned down.
sensesIntro.cn: subduct 的八个义项。主线是把某物引到下面：板块、水与沉积物这批货物，或向下转动的眼球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leading something under another surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：把某物引到另一表面之下。

branches.en: THE PLATE SINKS: the verb also works intransitively, so a plate can sink by itself.
branches.cn: 板块自行下沉：动词也可不及物，板块能凭自身重量下沉。

branches.en: SEDIMENT AND WATER: water, sediment and carbon travel down with the plate.
branches.cn: 沉积物与水：水、沉积物与碳随板块一起下行。

branches.en: SMALL DOWNWARD MOTION: medicine and surgery use the same direction at a human scale.
branches.cn: 小幅下移：医学与外科在人体尺度上使用同一方向。

branches.en: ASPECT: the participles separate the moving plate from the material already carried down.
branches.cn: 体貌：分词把正在运动的板片与已被带下去的物质分开。

branches.en: REMOVAL: what is led under stops belonging to the upper plate, so the crust is consumed rather than folded.
branches.cn: 移除：被带到下面的物质不再属于上覆板块，于是地壳被消减而不是被褶皱。

intro.en: Subduct is a Latin compound verb whose prefix, root and suffixes also build a large family of English words.
intro.cn: subduct 是拉丁复合动词，其前缀、词根与后缀还构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Sub- 'under' plus ducere 'to lead' gives subducere and the participle subductus; the same ducere family includes conduct, deduct and produce.
latinIntro.cn: sub-「在下」加 ducere「引导」构成 subducere 与分词 subductus；同一 ducere 词族还包括 conduct、deduct 与 produce。

items.example: The prefix fixes the downward direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀固定了向下的方向。

items.example: Conduct and produce share this root.
items.exampleCN: conduct 与 produce 共享这个词根。

items.meaning: in the act of descending beneath
items.example: The subducting slab bends at depth.
items.exampleCN: 俯冲板片在深处弯曲。

items.example: Subducted crust loses water as it heats.
items.exampleCN: 被俯冲的地壳在受热时失去水。

items.example: Subduction builds volcanic arcs.
items.exampleCN: 俯冲形成火山弧。

items.meaning: the finite form used with he, she or it
items.meaningCN: 与第三人称单数连用的限定形式
items.example: The older slab subducts faster.
items.exampleCN: 更古老的板片俯冲得更快。

items.meaning: to descend under a stated plate
items.example: The ocean plate subducts beneath the island arc.
items.exampleCN: 大洋板块俯冲到岛弧之下。

items.example: Only cold, dense lithosphere is readily subductable.
items.exampleCN: 只有寒冷致密的岩石圈才容易被俯冲。

definition_zh: 断层；过错；缺点；故障；责任
definition_en: a break in rock where one side has moved; also a mistake, a defect or responsibility for something wrong
core_image: 一层层岩体被拉开，两侧错位，形成一条可见的裂缝，裂缝两边的高度不再对齐
scene: 多年积累的应力终于释放，岩层沿一条裂缝突然错动。Movement along a fault released the strain that had built up for years.
sceneCN: 这里 fault 指「断层」（第 1 个义项：岩层两侧发生相对位移的破裂面）；句意为沿断层的运动释放了多年积累的应变。

pos.zh: 断层；过错；缺点；故障；责任
挑出……的毛病；使产生断层

collocations.phrase: through no fault of his own

senses.title: A break in rock
senses.titleCN: 断层：岩层破裂并发生位移
senses.definition: a break in rock along which one side has moved relative to the other
senses.definitionCN: 岩层中的破裂面，其一侧相对另一侧发生了移动
senses.example: Movement along a fault released the strain that had built up for years.
senses.exampleCN: 沿断层的运动释放了多年积累的应变。
senses.why: The geological sense comes from mining: a fault is where a seam of ore fails or is cut off.
senses.whyCN: 地质义来自采矿：断层就是矿层「断掉」或被截断的地方。

senses.title: A mistake or wrongdoing
senses.definition: a mistake or wrongful act
senses.definitionCN: 错误或不当的行为
senses.example: The delay was my fault, not yours.
senses.exampleCN: 延误是我的过错，不是你的。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is 'a failing or defect', which then attaches to the person who caused it.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项是「缺失或缺陷」，后来附到造成缺陷的人身上。

senses.title: A defect in character
senses.titleCN: 缺点：性格或事物上的缺陷
senses.definition: a weakness or flaw in a person's character or in a thing
senses.definitionCN: 人的性格或事物上的弱点、缺陷
senses.example: Generosity is his one fault as a negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 过于大方是他作为谈判者的唯一缺点。
senses.why: A fault is literally a break or gap, so an imperfect character is described as having a break in it.
senses.whyCN: fault 字面就是断裂或缺口，所以有缺陷的性格被描述为身上有一处断口。

senses.title: A technical fault
senses.titleCN: 故障：设备或系统的失灵
senses.definition: a failure in a machine, system or process
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或过程中的失灵
senses.example: A fault in the wiring cut the power.
senses.exampleCN: 线路故障切断了电力。
senses.why: A machine fails where a connection breaks, so the mining sense of a break survives in engineering.
senses.whyCN: 机器在连接断开处失灵，所以采矿中「断裂」的意思在工程里保留下来。

senses.title: Responsibility for something wrong
senses.definition: responsibility for a mistake or for something bad that happened
senses.definitionCN: 对错误或不幸事件应负的责任
senses.example: The driver was at fault in the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在这起事故中负有责任。
senses.why: If a fault is a defect, being at fault means the defect is located in you.
senses.whyCN: 如果 fault 是缺陷，那么 at fault 就意味着缺陷落在你身上。

senses.title: The fault plane
senses.titleCN: 断层面：断层两侧的接触面
senses.definition: the surface along which the two sides of a fault have slipped
senses.definitionCN: 断层两侧沿之滑动的面
senses.example: The fault plane dips steeply to the east.
senses.exampleCN: 断层面向东陡倾。
senses.why: Every fault has a surface of contact, so the noun extends to the geometry of that surface.
senses.whyCN: 每条断层都有一个接触面，因此这个名词也指该面的几何形态。

senses.title: A tennis service fault
senses.definition: in tennis, a serve that misses the legal area
senses.definitionCN: 网球中未落入合法区域的发球
senses.example: She served a fault and had to try again.
senses.exampleCN: 她发球失误，只好重发。
senses.why: The serve fails to land where it should, so the general 'failure' sense survives in sport.
senses.whyCN: 发球没有落到应在的位置，所以「失败」这一通用义在体育中保留下来。

senses.title: To find fault
senses.definition: to criticise small defects in someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对人或事物的小缺陷加以批评
senses.example: He finds fault with every plan we propose.
senses.exampleCN: 他挑我们提出的每一个方案的毛病。
senses.why: Finding fault is literally locating the defect, and the phrase shifted from diagnosis to complaint.
senses.whyCN: find fault 字面就是找出缺陷，这个短语从「诊断」转为「抱怨」。

intro.en: Fault comes from Latin fallere 'to deceive, fail' through Old French. The sense of a rock break grew out of mining language, where a seam 'fails'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fault 经古法语来自拉丁语 fallere「欺骗、失败」。岩石破裂义从采矿用语发展而来，那里矿层会「断掉」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fallere meant 'to deceive, disappoint, fail'; its past participle falsus gave false, and its noun sense of failure underlies fault.
items.cn: fallere 意为「欺骗、令人失望、失败」；其过去分词 falsus 产生 false，而「失败」的名词义构成 fault 的基础。

items.en: Old French faute meant 'a lack, a defect, a mistake'; the form lost the l and gained the sense of blame.
items.cn: 古法语 faute 意为「缺失、缺陷、错误」；这个词形丢了 l，并获得「责备」的意思。

items.en: Middle English restored an l under Latin influence, giving fault, and used it for defects of body, character and action.
items.cn: 中古英语在拉丁语影响下补回了 l，写成 fault，并用它指身体、性格与行为上的缺陷。

items.en: Miners called a break that cut off a seam a fault, and geologists adopted the term for any rock break with displacement.
items.cn: 矿工把截断矿层的断裂称为 fault，地质学家据此把这个词用于任何发生位移的岩石破裂。

items.en: Engineering added electrical and mechanical faults, sport added the tennis fault, and the phrase at fault fixed the sense of blame.
items.cn: 工程领域增加了电气与机械故障义，体育增加了网球发球失误义，短语 at fault 则固定了「担责」义。

items.en: The step from Latin fallere to Old French faute is generally accepted, but the exact medieval transmission is reconstructed rather than directly documented.
items.cn: 从拉丁语 fallere 到古法语 faute 这一步一般认为成立，但中古时期的具体传播路径是重构的，而非有直接文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to fault; group two holds words for defects and blame that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是形音接近 fault 的词；第二组是表示缺陷与责任但范围不同的词。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'defective'; fault is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「有缺陷的」形容词；fault 是名词。

entries.definition: an arched ceiling or a leap; it begins with /v/, not /f/.
entries.definitionCN: 拱顶，或跳跃；开头是 /v/ 而不是 /f/。

entries.definition: false or imitation, as in faux fur; it is a French borrowing without the final -lt.
entries.definitionCN: 假的、仿制的，如人造毛；它是法语借词，结尾没有 -lt。

entries.definition: failure to do something required, or an automatic setting; the de- prefix adds 'away from'.
entries.definitionCN: 未履行应做之事，或自动默认设置；前缀 de- 增添了「离开」的意思。

entries.definition: an imperfection in a product or a body; it stresses the missing quality rather than blame.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或身体上的不完美；它强调缺失的质量，而不是责备。

entries.definition: a weakness that may be hidden and may ruin something; it is often subtler than a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 可能隐蔽并毁掉某物的弱点；通常比 fault 更细微。

entries.definition: a wrong action or wrong result; it may be accidental and carries less blame than fault.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的行为或结果；可能是无意的，责备意味比 fault 轻。

entries.definition: responsibility for something bad; fault is the defect, blame is the judgement placed on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 对坏事的责任；fault 是缺陷，blame 是加在某人身上的评判。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the word's own history links rock breaks, defects and blame, so the senses can be held together by one image.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个词自身的历史把岩石破裂、缺陷与责备连在一起，因此各义项可用一个形象串起。

normal.en: A fault is a break: rock breaks, a machine breaks, a character has a break, and blame marks where the break is.
normal.cn: fault 就是断口：岩石断开、机器断开、性格有断口，而责备标明断口在哪里。

normal.en: Miners met a fault where a seam stopped, which is how the geological sense was born.
normal.cn: 矿工在矿层中断处遇到 fault，地质义就是这样诞生的。

normal.en: At fault means the defect is located in you, so responsibility follows the image.
normal.cn: at fault 表示缺陷落在你身上，责任便顺着这个形象而来。

normal.en: A tennis fault is a serve that fails to land in the right box, a small failure of the same kind.
normal.cn: 网球 fault 是发球没有落进正确区域，是同一类的小失败。

normal.en: Fault line and fault plane are both built from the geological sense, so learn them as a set.
normal.cn: fault line 与 fault plane 都出自地质义，可以成组记忆。

abstract.en: Abstractly, fault is a discontinuity: something that should be continuous is broken, whether rock, wire or character.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，fault 是一种不连续：本应连续的东西断了，无论是岩石、电线还是性格。

abstract.en: The word moves easily between the physical and the moral because both are read as breaks in a whole.
abstract.cn: 这个词在物理与道德之间移动自如，因为两者都被读作整体上的断口。

abstract.en: Symbol: two blocks offset along a diagonal seam, with a small arrow showing the slip.
abstract.cn: 符号：两块岩体沿一条斜缝错开，旁边一个小箭头表示滑动方向。

examples.en: The San Andreas Fault is a famous example of a transform fault.
examples.cn: 圣安德烈斯断层是一条著名的转换断层。

examples.en: The failure was not entirely his fault.
examples.cn: 这次失败并不完全是他的过错。

examples.en: Engineers traced the fault to a loose connector.
examples.cn: 工程师把故障追查到一处松动的接头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缝特」—— 岩层裂开一条特别的缝，两边错位 → fault 断层、过错

root: 源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失败），经古法语 faute 进入英语，核心含义是「缺失、断口」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fault. The core is a break or gap, which becomes a rock break, a defect, a machine failure or a blame.
sensesIntro.cn: fault 的八个义项。核心是断口或缺口，由此变成岩石破裂、缺陷、机器故障或责备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a break where two sides no longer line up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一处断口，两侧不再对齐。

branches.en: ROCK: a break with displacement, and the surface along which it slips.
branches.cn: 岩石：发生位移的破裂，以及沿之滑动的面。

branches.en: CHARACTER DEFECT: a weakness of character.
branches.cn: 性格缺陷：性格上的弱点。

branches.en: TENNIS FAULT: a serve misses the legal target.
branches.cn: 网球失误：发球未落入合法区域。

branches.en: BLAME: locating the defect in a person, and complaining about small defects.
branches.cn: 责备：把缺陷定位到某人身上，或对小缺陷加以抱怨。

branches.en: SMALL FAILURES: a wrong act and a machine glitch are both a small break in an expected order.
branches.cn: 小失败：做错一件事与机器出一次故障，都是应有秩序中的一个小断口。

intro.en: Fault has a small but productive family: two adjectives, a process noun and the prefixed word default.
intro.cn: fault 有一个小而能产的词族：两个形容词、一个过程名词，以及带前缀的 default。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is fallere 'to deceive, fail' and its participle falsus; Old French faute supplies the noun, and de- plus fallere gives default.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 fallere「欺骗、失败」及其分词 falsus；古法语 faute 提供名词，de- 加 fallere 构成 default。

items.example: The root also gives false and falsify.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也产生 false 与 falsify。

items.meaning: a missing quality or a wrong act
items.meaningCN: 缺失的品质或错误的行为
items.example: The French noun passed into English as fault.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词进入英语成为 fault。

items.meaningCN: 有缺陷的（-y 构成形容词）
items.example: The faulty cable caused the outage.
items.exampleCN: 有故障的电缆造成了停电。

items.meaningCN: 没有缺陷的（-less 表示无）
items.example: Her performance was faultless.
items.exampleCN: 她的表演无可挑剔。

items.meaning: the process of breaking and slipping in rock
items.meaningCN: 岩石破裂并滑动的过程
items.example: Faulting raised the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 断层作用抬起了山脊。

items.meaning: failure to act, or the standard setting
items.example: The system returned to its default.
items.exampleCN: 系统回到了默认设置。

items.example: The fault plane dips to the north.
items.exampleCN: 断层面向北倾。

items.meaning: a belt of broken rock around a fault
items.meaningCN: 断层周围破碎岩石构成的带
items.example: The fault zone is several kilometres wide.
items.exampleCN: 这条断层带宽达数公里。

items.meaning: the habit of criticising small defects
items.example: Constant fault-finding wore the team down.
items.exampleCN: 不断的挑剔使团队疲惫。

latinEntries.structure: falsus (perfect passive participle used as adjective)

definition_zh: 断层线；断层带在地表的位置；（比喻）分歧线、裂痕
definition_en: the line where a fault reaches the surface, or a figurative line of division
core_image: 地表上一条细长的裂缝，两边地面属于不同的岩块，裂缝沿线一字排开
scene: 地面上有一道细长的裂口，几个小镇沿着它分布。A row of small towns sits along the fault line, where the ground is cracked.
sceneCN: 这里 fault line 指「断层线」（第 1 个义项：断层在地表出露的位置）；句意为几个小镇沿着这条地面裂开的断层线分布。

pos.zh: 断层线；断层带；比喻分歧线

senses.title: The surface trace of a fault
senses.titleCN: 断层线：断层在地表的出露位置
senses.definition: the line along which a fault intersects the Earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 断层与地表相交的那条线
senses.example: A row of small towns sits along the fault line, where the ground is cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 几个小镇沿这条地面裂开的断层线分布。
senses.why: A fault is a surface in three dimensions; where it cuts the ground it appears as a line.
senses.whyCN: 断层是三维空间中的一个面；它切过地面时就表现为一条线。

senses.title: The fault zone
senses.definition: the belt of broken ground around a fault trace
senses.definitionCN: 断层迹线周围破碎地面构成的带
senses.example: Buildings inside the fault line were reinforced.
senses.exampleCN: 断层带内的建筑做了加固。
senses.why: In ordinary usage the line stands for the whole broken belt, because the damage is not confined to one metre.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法中，这条线代表整个破碎带，因为破坏并不限于一米宽。

senses.title: A seismic line
senses.definition: a line along which earthquakes are expected because a fault is active
senses.definitionCN: 因断层活动而预期发生地震的线
senses.example: The map marks every active fault line in red.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用红色标出每一条活动断层线。
senses.why: Active faults release strain repeatedly, so planning maps treat their traces as hazard lines.
senses.whyCN: 活动断层反复释放应变，因此规划图把它们的迹线当作灾害线。

senses.title: The mapped trace
senses.definition: the line drawn on a geological map to represent a fault
senses.definitionCN: 地质图上用来表示断层的那条线
senses.example: The fault line on the map is dashed where its position is uncertain.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上的断层线在位置不确定处画成虚线。
senses.why: Mapping reduces a three-dimensional surface to a symbol, and the symbol is a line.
senses.whyCN: 填图把三维的面简化为符号，而这个符号就是一条线。

senses.title: A line of weakness in a material
senses.definition: a line along which a material is likely to break
senses.definitionCN: 材料容易沿之断裂的线
senses.example: The crack followed a fault line in the cast metal.
senses.exampleCN: 裂缝沿着铸金属中的一条薄弱线扩展。
senses.why: The engineering use borrows the geological image for any prepared path of failure.
senses.whyCN: 工程用法借用地质形象，指任何预设的破坏路径。

senses.title: A political division
senses.definition: a figurative line separating opposed groups or opinions
senses.definitionCN: 分隔对立群体或意见的比喻性界线
senses.example: The treaty drew a new political fault line across the region.
